title: ammonites — Species Database
source: Ammonite Visual Database (English edition), non-NIMRF species; images hotlinked from Wikimedia Commons, open-access journals, USGS and Yale Peabody Museum | NIMRF Ammonite Visual Database Vol. 1 (National Rock, Mineral and Fossil Specimen Resource Sharing Platform, nimrf.net.cn)

species.classification: Order Agoniatitida / Family Agoniatitidae / Genus Agoniatites
species.distribution: Hamilton Group Mahantango Formation, Pennsylvania and New York, USA; the figured specimen was found by Michael Tomczyk in 2013 in Devonian strata about 385 million years old near Deer Lake, Pennsylvania. The genus also occurs in Algeria, Canada, the Czech Republic, Morocco, Russia and elsewhere (genus-level distribution).
species.diagnosis: A primitive ammonoid with a thin discoidal shell, a retrosiphonate ventral siphuncle (septal necks pointing backwards), and a goniatitic suture. It is the only ammonoid found in the Hamilton Group.
species.remarks: The order Agoniatitida (Ruzhencev, 1957) is a subjective synonym of Anarcestida (Miller & Furnish, 1954); Agoniatites also appears under the old name Anarcestes. Photo quality is average, but the species name was double-checked against the file name and the Wikipedia caption.

images.caption: Field specimen: a discoidal ammonoid embedded in rock, held in the discoverer's hand; found in Devonian strata near Deer Lake, Pennsylvania (2013). Photo quality is average. — Photo: Michael Tomczyk (Wikimedia Commons) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Agoniatitida / Family Agoniatitidae / Genus Agoniatites
species.age: Middle Devonian (the genus ranges from the Eifelian to the Givetian; this species occurs at the Eifelian/Givetian boundary section in Morocco)
species.distribution: Srbsko, Czech Republic (locality of the figured specimen, a museum slab in Paris-exhibition style); also recorded from the Jbel Ou Driss section, Ma'der region, Morocco.
species.diagnosis: Thin discoidal shell with a nearly smooth surface (genus characters: ventral siphuncle, goniatitic suture, a fast-swimming carnivorous ammonoid; species-level details not verified).
species.remarks: The species-author year is inconsistent: Bultynck's 1989 paper gives Agoniatites obliquus (WHIDBORNE, 1889), while the Korn & Klug 2002 caption gives (WHIDBORNE 1890); this entry follows 1889 and records the discrepancy. The species name was checked against the Commons file name and the species-level caption in the Wikidoc/Wikiversity mirror.

images.caption: Museum slab specimen: a large, thin discoidal ammonoid from Srbsko, Czech Republic. — Photo: Hectonichus (Wikimedia Commons) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Clymeniida / Family Clymeniidae / Genus Clymenia
species.genus_author: Münster, 1834 (Wikipedia infobox gives Swingle, 1939; see Remarks)
species.distribution: Poland (figured specimen: Góra Ostrówka, Gałęzice near Kielce, collected by J. Czarnocki); the species also occurs in Devonian strata of Australia, the United Kingdom and Morocco.
species.diagnosis: A closely coiled evolute shell with a smooth surface; the exceptionally rare dorsal siphuncle among all ammonoids (running along the inner side of the whorl); individuals from the L. styriacus Zone of Famennian Poland reach 15 cm in diameter.
species.remarks: The naming disputes must be kept side by side: the genus authority is given as Münster, 1834 (PBDB/Mindat and the Clymeniida classification table) and as Swingle, 1939 (Wikipedia genus-page infobox); the species-author year is given as 1839 (Wikipedia species page), 1831 (Korn & Klug 2002 caption) and 1832 (Conchology); this entry follows 1839. The museum label inside the photo is legible (Clymenia laevigata (Münster), Famennian, Polish locality), making this the strongest species-level evidence in this batch.

images.caption: Museum specimen: a coiled, smooth ammonoid; the label inside the photo is legible — Clymenia laevigata (Münster), Famennian, Góra Ostrówka, Poland (Gałęzice near Kielce), collected by J. Czarnocki. — Photo: Wikipek (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY 3.0)

species.classification: Order Clymeniida / Family Kosmoclymeniidae / Genus Kosmoclymenia
species.distribution: Sahara (locality of the figured Paris exhibit); the genus occurs in Devonian strata of China, Germany and Morocco.
species.diagnosis: Genus characters: shell reaching up to 110 mm in maximum diameter, a fast-swimming carnivore; the figure shows two specimens side by side on a green background. Species-level details not verified.
species.remarks: The full form in the Wikipedia Kosmoclymenia genus-page infobox caption is Kosmoclymenia (Muessenbiaergia) bisulcata, from the Sahara, now in the Paris Gallery of Comparative Anatomy and Palaeontology; this entry uses the short form and records the subgenus information here. The species-author year is not verified and is not inferred.

images.caption: Two coiled ammonoid specimens side by side on a green background, exhibits of the Paris Gallery of Comparative Anatomy and Palaeontology, from the Sahara. Note: there are two specimens in the figure. — Photo: Author not verified (Wikimedia Commons) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Clymeniida / Family Cymaclymeniidae / Genus Cymaclymenia
species.age: Late Devonian, Famennian (Famennian of Germany; also recorded from the late Famennian Effenbergia lens Zone at Dzikowiec, Poland)
species.distribution: Germany (Famennian); Dzikowiec, Poland; also recorded from Dasbergian strata in the Carnic Alps.
species.diagnosis: Shell surface with rather coarse, bundled growth lines and weak ribs around the umbilicus; one of the commonest species of the genus. The figured specimen is heavily worn, so detail is limited.
species.remarks: The species-level evidence is mainly the small handwritten label “C. striata” inside the photo; the specimen itself is worn and the photo is weak in detail, as the caption states. Family placement follows the Cyrtoclymeniaceae superfamily member list (Cymaclymeniidae is one of its member families).

images.caption: A worn discoidal specimen in a tray, with a small handwritten label “C. striata” inside the photo; detail is weak, and the species name rests mainly on that label and the file name. — Photo: Author not verified (Wikimedia Commons) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Clymeniida / Family Kosmoclymeniidae / Genus Kosmoclymenia
species.distribution: Upper Franconia, Germany (originally described area); also recorded from the Carnic Alps; the genus occurs in Devonian strata of China, Germany and Morocco.
species.diagnosis: Genus characters: shell reaching up to 110 mm in maximum diameter, a fast-swimming carnivore; the figure is a worn, large coiled specimen. Species-level details not verified.
species.remarks: The original combination was Planulites undulatus Münster, 1832, later transferred to Clymenia (1834) and then to Kosmoclymenia (per the synonymy table in Korn & Price 1987). There is no label in the figure, and the species name rests on the Commons file name; the caption states this limitation. Gümbel in 1863 historically lumped many Kosmoclymenia into undulata; this broad historical usage is not listed as a synonym. Added 2026-11-05: the National Rock, Mineral and Fossil Specimen Resource Sharing Platform holds a specimen under the same name (Chengdu University of Technology Museum, specimen no. 7924000.0), its label reading Bōwén yǔzhòu hǎishénshí (“rippled cosmic sea-god stone”), matching this species name; its photograph is included as the second figure on this page (carries the platform's watermark; licence for use still to be confirmed).

images.caption: A worn, large coiled specimen in a tray; there is no label in the figure, and the species name rests on the Commons file name — weaker evidence than a labelled specimen. — Photo: Author not verified (Wikimedia Commons) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Clymeniida / Family Clymeniidae / Genus Clymenia
species.genus_author: Münster, 1834 (Wikipedia infobox gives Swingle, 1939; see Remarks)
species.age: Late Devonian (the genus is restricted to the Late Devonian; the exact horizon of this species is not verified)
species.distribution: Devonian strata of Europe (per Nicholson 1876: Clymenia occurs in Europe; the genus occurs in Europe and Western Australia).
species.diagnosis: Genus characters: discoidal shell, only weakly lobed septa, siphuncle on the inner (dorsal) margin of the septa; the figure is a historical engraving of a finely ribbed evolute shell. Species-level details not verified.
species.remarks: The figure is a 19th-century historical engraving (of the same kind as the C. sedgwickii illustrations published by Dana 1863 and Figuier 1867); there is no label in the figure, and the species name rests on the Commons file name; the species author and year are both not verified and are not inferred. The Wikipedia Clymenia genus-page species list includes this species. The genus-author dispute is the same as in the Clymenia laevigata entry.

images.caption: Historical engraving: a finely ribbed evolute discoidal shell; there is no label in the figure, and the species name rests on the Commons file name — weaker evidence than a labelled specimen. — Photo: Author not verified (Wikimedia Commons, 19th-century historical engraving) (Commons free media (exact CC variant not shown))

species.classification: Order Goniatitida / Superfamily Goniatitaceae / Family Goniatitidae / Subfamily Goniatitinae
species.age: Carboniferous, about 345.3–326.4 million years ago; the photographed specimen comes from Viséan strata (label reads “Wizen”)
species.distribution: Poland (photographed specimen: Jugów, near Ząbkowice Śląskie, collected by H. Żakowa); also recorded from Culm strata of Germany (Hesse, Nassau, Westphalia, Harz), Belgium, the United Kingdom, Ireland and Moravia, per the 1870 Quarterly Journal of the Geological Society of London.
species.diagnosis: A fast-swimming carnivorous ammonoid (per Wikipedia, citing the Paleobiology Database). Genus characters: shell generally globular, umbilicus open but narrow, shell surface often reticulate where longitudinal ridges meet transverse striae; the ventral lobe of the suture is rather narrow with a median saddle, and the first lateral saddle is nearly to fully angular.
species.remarks: The label in the photo directly gives the species name, the Viséan age and the Jugów locality, and is the direct evidence for identifying this species. The suborder is not stated in the sources read, so it is not included in the classification string.

images.caption: Two Goniatites crenistria specimens from Jugów, Poland, displayed in a museum case; the label gives the Viséan age (“Wizen”) and H. Żakowa as collector. — Photo: Not verified (Wikimedia Commons) (Not verified (Wikimedia Commons free licence, exact licence unverified))

species.classification: Order Goniatitida / Suborder Tornoceratina / Superfamily Tornoceratoidea / Family Tornoceratidae / Subfamily Tornoceratinae
species.age: Middle Devonian (photographed specimen: Alden Pyrite Bed, Ludlowville Formation, New York State); the genus ranges from the Middle to the Late Devonian
species.distribution: Alden Pyrite Bed (Ludlowville Formation, Middle Devonian), western New York State, USA; the original combination Goniatites uniangularis Conrad, 1842 was collected in New York State.
species.synonyms: Goniatites uniangularis Conrad, 1842 (original combination; note the spelling difference between uniangularis and the current uniangulare)
species.diagnosis: Genus characters (Korn & Bockwinkel 2022 genus diagnosis): compressed shell, umbilicus slightly open in the juvenile stage and closed in the pre-adult stage, generally no ventral groove, biconvex growth lines without ribs; suture formula E A L I, adventitious lobe broad, rounded, asymmetrical and steep on the dorsal side. Strongly involute, near-discoidal shell, with the suture forming 6–10 lobes.
species.remarks: The figured specimens are of the aldenense form, not the nominate subspecies, as the captions state. The author's own website (jsjgeology.net) labels them only as Tornoceras uniangulare, without a variety name; the aldenense determination rests on the locality and morphology information supplied for this task, and the form note in the captions should be retained when compiling. Also note the spelling variants: Korn & Bockwinkel 2022 write House's 1965 variety as aldanense, while the task source writes aldenense — both spellings coexist.

images.caption: Pyritized Tornoceras uniangulare internal mould, side view, 2.7 cm in diameter — Alden Pyrite Bed specimen, aldenense form, not the nominate subspecies. — Photo: James St. John (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY 2.0)
Axial view of the same specimen, showing the serrated suture — Alden Pyrite Bed specimen, aldenense form, not the nominate subspecies. — Photo: James St. John (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY 2.0)

species.classification: Order Goniatitida / Family Gattendorfiidae / Subfamily Gattendorfiinae
species.age: Early Carboniferous, early Tournaisian, Gattendorfia Limestone bed 21, near the Devonian–Carboniferous boundary
species.distribution: Old quarry at Gattendorf, Upper Franconia, Germany (400 m northwest of the Kirchgattendorf church, Gattendorfia Limestone bed 21, type locality).
species.synonyms: Goniatites subinvolutus Münster, 1839 (original combination); Gattendorfia ventroplana Schindewolf, 1924 (plate caption dated 1923; synonymized with this species by Korn & Weyer 2023)
species.diagnosis: Shell reaching 90 mm; at 80 mm thinly discoidal and subevolute (ww/dm about 0.40, uw/dm about 0.40), whorl weakly compressed (ww/wh about 1.10), low whorl expansion rate (WER about 1.70), venter broadly rounded, umbilical margin narrowly rounded; growth lines lamellar, widely spaced and convex towards growth, with short ribs at the umbilical margin; no shell constrictions and no internal shell thickening. The absence of shell constrictions is precisely what distinguishes this species from most others in the genus.
species.remarks: The holotype is poorly preserved (80 mm, weathered, no shell material remaining), but it is the type of this species. Note the distinction: Oberrödinghausen material previously assigned to this species by Vöhringer (1960) and Korn (1994) has fine shell constrictions and a broader shell and has been separated as Gattendorfia rhenana Korn & Weyer, 2023 — it does not belong to this species. Superfamily and suborder are not stated for this genus alone in the sources read, so they are not included in the classification string; Korn & Weyer 2023 place Gattendorfiidae among the prionoceratid group. This species is the type species of the genus Gattendorfia.

images.caption: Figure 25 from Korn & Weyer 2023: panel A is the holotype of Gattendorfia subinvoluta (SNSB BSPG AS VII 30, Münster Collection), side view, from Gattendorf, Germany, 80 mm shell diameter (full figure plate shown). — Photo: Korn & Weyer, 2023 (European Journal of Taxonomy 883, Fig. 25) (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Goniatitida / Family Prionoceratidae / Subfamily Acutimitoceratinae
species.age: Early Carboniferous, early Tournaisian, Gattendorfia Limestone bed 21
species.distribution: Old quarry at Gattendorf, Upper Franconia, Germany (bed 21, type locality); also reported from the Oberrödinghausen area in the Rhineland (per the material described in that paper).
species.synonyms: Imitoceras intermedium Schindewolf, 1923 (original combination); Acutimitoceras intermedium (later combination)
species.diagnosis: Shell reaching 120 mm; at 5 mm thinly to thickly discoidal and subinvolute to subevolute (ww/dm about 0.70, uw/dm 0.20–0.40); at 15–30 mm thinly to thickly discoidal and involute (ww/dm about 0.65, umbilicus nearly closed), whorl weakly compressed (ww/wh 1.10–1.20), medium to high whorl expansion rate (WER 1.85–1.95), venter broadly rounded, umbilical margin extremely broadly rounded; growth lines lamellar and widely spaced, convexly arched on the flanks and forming a broad, deep ventral sinus.
species.remarks: This species is an off-list addition, not a species on the original candidate list; it is included to bring this batch to 5 species because its plate licence is verified and its classification is clear — compilers who wish to restrict strictly to the original candidate list may remove it. The figure is specimen BGRB X13384 (60 mm) in Fig. 8C, side view, not the holotype/lectotype; the lectotype is SMF Mbg.3111 (Fig. 8A), which is poorly preserved and deformed in the last half whorl, so a clearer specimen of the same species was chosen. Suborder and superfamily are not stated for this genus alone in the sources read, so they are not included in the classification string.

images.caption: Figure 8 from Korn & Weyer 2023: panel C is specimen BGRB X13384 of Stockumites intermedius (Schindewolf 1934 Collection), side view, from Gattendorf bed 21, Germany, 60 mm shell diameter (full figure plate shown). — Photo: Korn & Weyer, 2023 (European Journal of Taxonomy 883, Fig. 8) (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Goniatitida / Family Prionoceratidae / Subfamily Prionoceratinae
species.age: Early Carboniferous, early Tournaisian, Gattendorfia Limestone bed 21 (Acutimitoceras ucatum Zone, inferred per Korn & Weyer 2023; zone name as in the original)
species.distribution: Old quarry at Gattendorf, Upper Franconia, Germany (bed 21, type locality).
species.diagnosis: At 20–30 mm thickly discoidal and subinvolute (ww/dm 0.80–0.85), whorl section compressed, low whorl expansion rate (WER about 1.70); ornament of rather coarse, sharp, densely spaced, weakly biconvex growth lines with prominent biconvex shell constrictions. The lectotype, 19 mm, is thickly discoidal (ww/dm 0.83) with a clearly closed umbilicus, flanks and venter nearly semicircularly arched, constrictions and coarse growth lines both weakly biconvex, lateral sinus extremely shallow and ventral sinus slightly deeper and narrow.
species.remarks: This species is also an off-list addition, not on the original candidate list; it is included to bring this batch to 5 species because its plate licence is verified and its classification is clear — compilers who wish to restrict strictly to the original candidate list may remove it. Note the distinction: globular Oberrödinghausen material formerly called Imitoceras varicosum / Mimimitoceras varicosum has been separated by Korn & Weyer 2023 as Mimimitoceras perditum and does not belong to this species; the “non” entries in that paper's synonymy list are all misidentifications and are not treated as synonyms. The figure is paralectotype SMF Mbg.7560 (28 mm) in Fig. 4A, side view, not the lectotype (lectotype SMF Mbg.4706 in Fig. 4B, 19 mm); the larger specimen was chosen for easier reading by children. Suborder and superfamily are not stated for this genus alone in the sources read, so they are not included in the classification string.

images.caption: Figure 4 from Korn & Weyer 2023: panel A is paralectotype SMF Mbg.7560 of Mimimitoceras varicosum (Schindewolf 1916 Collection), side view, from Gattendorf bed 21, Germany, about 28 mm shell diameter (full figure plate shown). — Photo: Korn & Weyer, 2023 (European Journal of Taxonomy 883, Fig. 4) (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Prolecanitida / Family Prolecanitidae / Subfamily Prolecanitinae
species.age: Early Carboniferous, early Tournaisian (Mississippian), Hangenberg Limestone (Gattendorfia Limestone)
species.distribution: Hangenberg Limestone of the Oberrödinghausen railway cutting, Rhenish Mountains, Germany (locality of the holotype and supplementary material).
species.diagnosis: Shell reaching 35 mm in diameter; at 12 mm shell diameter evolute (umbilical width/shell diameter about 0.50), whorl slightly depressed (width/height about 1.05), venter broadly rounded; at 30 mm still evolute, whorl slightly compressed (width/height about 0.90), venter broadly rounded. Ornament of coarse, strongly backward-bent, biconvex, crenulated growth lines with a deep ventral sinus; no ribs, no nodes. The external lobe of the suture is lanceolate, and the adventitious lobe is asymmetrical and dorsally sac-shaped.
species.remarks: Holotype GZG.INV.1689, designated by Vöhringer (1960); the original figure of Schmidt (1925), plate 23, fig. 2, is reprinted as panel D in this plate. Panels A–C are Oberrödinghausen specimens (GPIT-PV-63968, GPIT-PV-63972, MB.C.31234.1), and D is a reprint of the 1925 original figure. Eocanites is one of the genera with the simplest sutures in the entire order Prolecanitida; the genus distribution (genus-level) also includes Montagne Noire in France, Thuringia, Lower Silesia, the Carnic Alps, Guizhou in China, the Anti-Atlas of Morocco, and other places.

images.caption: Figure 119 from Korn & Weyer 2023: plate of Eocanites nodosus — A. specimen GPIT-PV-63968, bed 3d; B. specimen GPIT-PV-63972, bed 3d; C. specimen MB.C.31234.1, bed 3d1b; D. reprint of Schmidt (1925) plate 23, fig. 2. Scale unit 1 mm. — Photo: Korn & Weyer 2023, European Journal of Taxonomy 882, Fig. 119 (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Prolecanitida / Family Prolecanitidae / Subfamily Prolecanitinae
species.species_etymology: Latin delicatus, referring to the delicate ornament
species.age: Early Carboniferous, early Tournaisian (Mississippian), Hangenberg Limestone (Gattendorfia Limestone)
species.distribution: Hangenberg Limestone of the Oberrödinghausen railway cutting, Rhenish Mountains, Germany (holotype bed 1, paratype beds 1–2, and loose material).
species.diagnosis: Shell reaching 60 mm in diameter; at 12 mm shell diameter evolute (umbilical width/shell diameter about 0.55), whorl slightly depressed (width/height about 1.10), venter broadly rounded; at 30 mm evolute (umbilical width/shell diameter about 0.50), whorl nearly circular (width/height about 1.00), venter broadly rounded. Ornament of fine, backward-bent, concavo-convex growth lines, ventral sinus of medium depth, and low, rounded folds on the flanks. The external lobe of the suture is slightly sac-shaped, and the adventitious lobe is lanceolate and slightly sac-shaped. The holotype, 42.3 mm, is extremely thinly discoidal with a wide umbilicus (width/shell diameter about 0.23–0.25, umbilical width/shell diameter about 0.50).
species.remarks: This species is a new species established by Korn & Weyer (2023) from the Oberrödinghausen material; the holotype GPIT-PV-63997 was misassigned by Vöhringer (1960) to Eocanites supradevonicus, from which this species differs by its weaker ornament and slightly narrower umbilicus. Panel A is the holotype (embedded in matrix), panel B is paratype MB.C.31247.1.

images.caption: Figure 125 from Korn & Weyer 2023: plate of Eocanites delicatus — A. holotype GPIT-PV-63997, bed 1; B. paratype MB.C.31247.1, horizon not specified. Scale unit 1 mm. — Photo: Korn & Weyer 2023, European Journal of Taxonomy 882, Fig. 125 (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ceratitida / Family Ceratitidae / Subfamily Ceratitinae
species.age: Middle Triassic, latest upper Anisian to early Ladinian; the figured specimen is from the German Upper Muschelkalk
species.distribution: Found only in the Germanic Basin, i.e. the partly isolated shallow sea stretching from eastern France, north of the future Alps, to Poland.
species.diagnosis: Discoidal shell with ribbed flanks, ribs more widely spaced on the last whorl; adult venter rounded and smooth, juvenile venter grooved; ceratitic suture (smooth saddles and serrated lobes).
species.remarks: Naming note: Urlichs (1991, in Case 2732 submitted to the International Commission on Zoological Nomenclature) proposed attributing the current name Ceratites nodosus to Schlotheim 1813 and designating a lectotype, to preserve the current meaning in use since 1901; Bruguière's 1789 Ammonites nodosa refers to something else under the current name (= Ceratites robustus robustus), and the material described by Schlotheim in 1813/1820 is in fact a mixture of at least 15 currently recognised species, so this entry records the species author as Schlotheim 1813 and explains the dispute here. The figure is the Toulouse Museum specimen MHNT.PAL.CEP.2001.105; an old collection label with the handwritten words Ceratites nodosus, Muschelkalk, Württemberg is visible at the lower right.

images.caption: Ceratites nodosus fossil, German Upper Muschelkalk specimen, Toulouse Museum collection (MHNT.PAL.CEP.2001.105); an old collection label is at the lower right. — Photo: Didier Descouens (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY-SA 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ceratitida / Family Meekoceratidae
species.distribution: Early Triassic marine strata of western North America and Alaska; the figured plate specimens were collected at USGS Mesozoic locality M5027, upper Chulitna district, Alaska.
species.diagnosis: Compressed discoidal shell with flat flanks, narrow, flat or rounded venter, without keel or groove; surface smooth or with lateral folds, without nodes, spines or spiral ridges; umbilicus of varying size, short body chamber; ceratitic suture with smooth, rounded saddles and serrated lobes. This species is the type species of the genus Meekoceras.
species.remarks: Classification dispute note: this entry treats it under Meekoceratidae (both Smith 1932 and Arkell et al. 1957 place Meekoceras in that family); however, the family placement of Meekoceras is disputed in different works, with another classification placing it in Prionitidae, and no ruling is made here. Higher-level placement is also disputed: Arkell et al. 1957 place Meekoceratidae in Noritoidea, Smith 1932 in Prolecanitoidea. The figured specimen is YPM IP 028177, Yale Peabody Museum (photo: J. Utrup, 2013).

images.caption: Meekoceras gracilitatis specimen YPM IP 028177, Yale Peabody Museum (photo: J. Utrup, 2013) — lateral and ventral views. — Photo: Yale Peabody Museum, CC0 (photo: J. Utrup, 2013) (CC0)

species.classification: Order Ceratitida / Family Ceratitidae / Subfamily Beyrichitinae
species.age: Middle Triassic, late Anisian (Fossil Hill Member; index fossil of the Gymnotoceras rotelliformis Zone)
species.distribution: Fossil Hill Member of the Fossil Hill area, Humboldt Range, and Muller Canyon, Augusta Mountains, northwestern Nevada, USA; the figured specimen is held in the geological collection of the University of Bremen, Germany (GSUB).
species.diagnosis: Stout discoidal shell with an extremely weak keel; regular, slightly forward-inclined ribs that weaken near adulthood; rounded ventral shoulders; about 6 whorls, maximum diameter about 34.3 mm.
species.remarks: This species is the index fossil of the late Anisian Gymnotoceras rotelliformis Zone. The figure is a crop of the lower row (M–P) of Fig. 4 in Bischof et al. 2021, showing side and edge views of two specimens (GSUB C11594, C11702), including a 2 cm scale bar. Note: this genus and species are traditionally difficult to distinguish from close relatives on morphology alone, and the original paper also notes that several specimens at different growth stages are needed for reliable identification; this entry follows the original paper's identification.

images.caption: Gymnotoceras rotelliformis (original paper Fig. 4 M–P): side and edge views of two specimens, 2 cm scale bar; crop of the lower row of the original figure. — Photo: Bischof et al. 2021, PeerJ (CC BY) (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Family Dactylioceratidae
species.distribution: Canada, France, Italy, Russia, Serbia and Montenegro, the United Kingdom, the United States; the figured specimen was collected from the Whitby Formation on the Yorkshire coast, England.
species.synonyms: Ammonites communis Sowerby, 1815 (original combination, type species of the genus)
species.diagnosis: Shell with straight or slightly convex ribs crossing the venter; ribs on the outer whorl more robust; whorl section circular. The figured specimen is about 5 cm wide.
species.remarks: The figured specimen is a “snakestone”: the snake head at the top was carved by later hands, following the folk custom of the Whitby St Hilda snake-driving legend — it is not part of the ammonoid's anatomy. Note: shell-diameter figures in the genus-page sources disagree (9–11 cm versus an average of 24.1 mm), and this book does not adopt the disputed shell-diameter figures.

images.caption: Snakestone: a Dactylioceras commune fossil with a snake head carved at the upper right — a man-made carving from Whitby folklore, not part of the ammonoid's anatomy. The specimen comes from the Whitby Formation on the Yorkshire coast, England, Lower Jurassic. — Photo: James St. John (Wikimedia Commons / Flickr) (CC BY 2.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ammonitina / Superfamily Hildoceratoidea / Family Hildoceratidae / Subfamily Harpoceratinae
species.age: Early Jurassic, Toarcian (Falciferum Zone to Commune Subzone of the Bifrons Zone)
species.distribution: Lower Jurassic of Europe, North Africa, Russia, Japan, Borneo, New Zealand, Indonesia, North America and South America.
species.synonyms: Ammonites falcifer Sowerby, 1820 (original combination, type species of the genus)
species.diagnosis: A relatively fast-swimming carnivore; H. serpentinum and H. falciferum are important index fossils of the Toarcian.
species.remarks: The figure for this species is a life restoration illustration, not a fossil photograph, as the caption states.

images.caption: Life restoration illustration (not a fossil photograph): a Harpoceras falciferum catching a small shrimp-like animal with its tentacles, against blue seawater. — Photo: NobuTamura (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY-SA 3.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Family Amaltheidae
species.age: Early Jurassic, late Pliensbachian (upper Pliensbachian), about 189.6–183 million years ago
species.distribution: France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Serbia and Montenegro, Spain, the United Kingdom; the figured specimen was collected near Unterstürmig in northern Bavaria, Germany.
species.synonyms: Ammonites costatus Schlotheim, 1820; Ammonites franconicus Schlotheim, 1813
species.diagnosis: Flat discoidal (planulate) shell, whorl section nearly square, with robust radial ribs ending in nodes at the outer ventral margin; venter flat with a strongly serrated keel; shell diameter about 45–54 mm; species of this genus were fast-swimming carnivores.
species.remarks: The figured specimen is the counterpart (negative mould) of a pyritized specimen, about 3.85 cm at its widest; the golden appearance comes from the shell having been replaced by pyrite (“fool's gold”).

images.caption: Pyritized Pleuroceras spinatum fossil counterpart (negative mould), with a golden-silver shell bearing robust radial ribs; the specimen was collected near Unterstürmig in northern Bavaria, Germany, about 3.85 cm at its widest. — Photo: James St. John (Wikimedia Commons / Flickr) (CC BY 2.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Family Stephanoceratidae
species.age: Middle Jurassic, lower Bajocian, about 170–168 million years ago
species.distribution: Canada, Mexico, Saudi Arabia, Spain; S. humphriesianum also occurs in the United Kingdom and Germany; the figured specimen was collected from the Humphriesianum Zone of the Inferior Oolite at Clatcombe, Dorset, England.
species.synonyms: Ammonites humphriesianum J. de C. Sowerby, 1825 (original combination, type species of the genus)
species.diagnosis: Evolute shell with well-developed, node-bearing ribs; primary ribs arise from the umbilical seam and bifurcate on the flanks (occasionally trifurcate), secondary ribs crossing the venter without interruption; nodes at the bifurcation points; shell diameter up to 27 cm, outer whorl width up to 6 cm; sexually dimorphic (macroconch and microconch).
species.remarks: Spelling note: variant spellings such as humphreysianum also occur; this book uses humphriesianum. The figured specimen is 275 mm long, from the Humphriesianum Zone at Clatcombe, Dorset. This species did not use the previously planned Haeckel plate 44 route (the plate file could not be verified); the Clatcombe specimen photograph from the Wikipedia image library is used instead.

images.caption: Stephanoceras humphriesianum fossil displayed on a base, with fine radial ribs and the evolute shell form clearly visible; the specimen comes from the Inferior Oolite Humphriesianum Zone at Clatcombe, Dorset, England, 275 mm long. — Photo: Micktherocktapper (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY-SA 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Family Douvilleiceratidae
species.age: Early Cretaceous, lower Albian (Mammillatum Zone); the genus generally ranges from the Barremian to the Cenomanian, most typically Albian
species.distribution: Angola, Brazil, Canada, Colombia, Dominican Republic, Egypt, France, Iran, Japan, Madagascar, Mexico, Peru, South Africa, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, the United States (Alaska, Texas) and elsewhere; this species is a cosmopolitan lower Albian index fossil (Mammillatum Zone).
species.diagnosis: The illustrated figure shows a shell with robust radial ribs bearing nodes and broad whorls; this species is the index fossil of the lower Albian Mammillatum Zone.
species.remarks: The figure is a black-and-white scientific illustration (Ernst Haeckel, Kunstformen der Natur, 1904), not a fossil photograph; the illustration style is somewhat exaggerated, emphasizing ribs and nodes over realism. Classification note: the Wikipedia genus page places this family under the suborder Ancyloceratina, but another classification places it in Ammonitina; this book lists only to family level. Genus-author year: Wikipedia gives 1894, ICZN Opinion 422 gives 1893. The species spellings mammillatum/mamillare both occur in historical literature; ICZN Opinion 422 follows the neotype designated by Casey (1954).

images.caption: Black-and-white scientific illustration of Douvilleiceras mammillatum (Ernst Haeckel, Kunstformen der Natur, 1904), showing robust, node-bearing radial ribs; this is an illustration, not a fossil photograph. — Photo: Ernst Haeckel (Wikimedia Commons) (PD-old)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Family Hoplitidae / Subfamily Cleoniceratinae
species.age: Early Cretaceous, lower Albian to basal middle Albian (Lower to basal Middle Albian), about 113–100 million years ago
species.distribution: Europe, Madagascar, the Transcaspian region; the figured specimen is a private-collection specimen from the lower Albian of Madagascar.
species.synonyms: Cleoniceras besairei (spelling variant, in the genus-page species list)
species.diagnosis: A rather involute, high-whorled Hoplitidae; small umbilicus; venter arched to sharp; typical falcate ribs arising in pairs from umbilical nodes and fading towards the outer whorl.
species.remarks: The figured specimen shows iridescent nacre, a common preservation feature of Madagascar specimens. The genus-author year is also given as 1897 elsewhere; this book follows the Wikipedia genus page's 1895.

images.caption: Cleoniceras besairiei fossil with iridescent nacre on the shell surface and the inner whorls clearly visible; the specimen comes from the lower Albian of Madagascar. — Photo: Antonov (Wikimedia Commons) (PD)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Superfamily Acanthoceratoidea / Family Brancoceratidae / Subfamily Mortoniceratinae
species.age: Early Cretaceous, middle to upper Albian (middle and upper Albian); the Mortoniceras inflatum Zone belongs to the lower upper Albian
species.distribution: Algeria, Angola, Armenia, Belgium, Canada (British Columbia), Colombia, Ecuador, France, Germany, Iran, Japan, Madagascar, Mexico, Mozambique, Myanmar, Nigeria, South Africa, Spain, Suriname, Switzerland, Ukraine, the United Kingdom, the United States (California, New Mexico, Texas, Oregon), Venezuela; the figured specimen was collected at Ndumu, South Africa, and is now in the Natural History Museum, Berlin.
species.diagnosis: The figured specimen is about 20 cm in diameter, with robust radial ribs and nodes on the shell surface (see figure); specimens of this genus reach up to 30 cm in diameter.
species.remarks: The figured specimen is a collection of the Natural History Museum, Berlin, collected at Ndumu, South Africa, upper Albian; this species is the zonal fossil of the upper Albian Mortoniceras inflatum Zone.

images.caption: Mortoniceras inflatum fossil on a black background, with coarse ribs and nodes clearly visible on the shell surface; the specimen is about 20 cm in diameter, collected at Ndumu, South Africa, upper Albian, now in the Natural History Museum, Berlin. — Photo: H. Zell (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY-SA 3.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ammonitina / Superfamily Desmoceratoidea / Family Desmoceratidae / Subfamily Puzosiinae
species.age: Late Cretaceous, Santonian to lower Campanian (Santonian–lower Campanian); the figured lectotype specimen was collected near Seppenrade, Germany, in 1894
species.distribution: United Kingdom, France, Germany, North America (154 specimens studied); the largest known ammonite species.
species.diagnosis: Moderately involute shell with flat or slightly rounded flanks; inner whorls with distinct primary and secondary ribs; gigantic size, generally over 60 cm.
species.remarks: Size wording must stay accurate: the 1895 Seppenrade specimen measured 1.74 m in diameter (some sources give 1.8 m); because part of the body chamber is missing, the complete reconstruction is about 2.05 m; never shorten this to “measured 2 m”. The figure is a photograph of the lectotype specimen, now in the LWL Natural History Museum, Münster — not the previously planned cast (Abguss) image, whose file name could not be verified in this batch, so the lectotype photograph from the PLOS open-access paper is used instead.

images.caption: Photograph of the lectotype specimen: Parapuzosia seppenradensis collected near Seppenrade, Germany, now in the LWL Natural History Museum, Münster; scale bar at lower left is 100 mm. — Photo: C. Ifrim  et al. (PLOS ONE, 2021), photo: CI (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Superfamily Hoplitoidea / Family Placenticeratidae
species.species_etymology: Named for American palaeontologist Fielding Bradford Meek
species.age: Late Cretaceous, Campanian, about 80 million years ago
species.distribution: Mainly the Western Interior Seaway of western North America; the figured specimen was collected from the Pierre Shale near Pueblo, Colorado, USA, and is now in the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History.
species.diagnosis: Discoidal, involute, laterally compressed shell; shell diameter generally 20–50 cm, up to 1 m; the shell surface is often covered with opalized nacre (ammolite).
species.remarks: The figured specimen bears paired bite marks on both sides, judged to have been left by a mosasaur. Note: the original image is low resolution (379×340) and should not be enlarged in print. The genus-author year is given as both 1870 and 1876; this book follows the Wikipedia genus page's 1870.

images.caption: Placenticeras meeki specimen, with paired round bite marks visible on both sides (judged to be mosasaur bite marks); the specimen comes from the Campanian Pierre Shale near Pueblo, Colorado, now in the Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History. Note: the original image is low resolution. — Photo: USGS (Public Domain)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ancyloceratina / Superfamily Turrilitaceae / Family Baculitidae
species.distribution: Western Interior Seaway of North America: upper Pierre Shale in southwestern South Dakota, USA, upper Pierre Shale near Trinidad, Colorado; related material also occurs in the Bearpaw Formation of western Canada.
species.diagnosis: A straight-shelled (baculiform) ammonoid, large; compared with its close relative Baculites baculus, the shell cross-section is more oval and the individual slightly larger, up to 10.2 cm in diameter; the suture is similar to that of B. baculus; per the NMGS 2018 account, its cross-section is nearly triangular.
species.remarks: One of the index fossils of the lower Maastrichtian of the Western Interior Seaway, its fossil zone lying above the B. baculus Zone; cast photographs from the North American Museum of Ancient Life are among the commonest baculite images.

images.caption: Cast of a Baculites grandis shell exhibited at the North American Museum of Ancient Life (Lehi, Utah, USA). — Photo: Ninjatacoshell (Wikimedia Commons) (CC BY-SA 3.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ancyloceratina / Family Nostoceratidae
species.age: Late Cretaceous, Coniacian (Japan); possibly extending to the Turonian of Madagascar
species.distribution: Mainly the Upper Cretaceous of Japan; N. mirabilis occurs in Coniacian strata of Japan and possibly in Turonian strata of Madagascar.
species.diagnosis: An extremely peculiar shell form: the early part consists of several open coiled whorls, followed by a series of alternating U-shaped bends around the early whorls, forming oxbow-like curves that look tangled; ribs oblique and parallel to the position of the old aperture; suture type not verified.
species.remarks: The tangled-looking shell form in fact follows regular segmented geometry; it is one of the symbolic fossils of the Palaeontological Society of Japan; hydrostatic modelling studies show it could still achieve neutral buoyancy and did not have to live on the sea floor.

images.caption: Virtual restoration of the Nipponites mirabilis shell (CT-scanned 3D model): A. 3D model; B. restored body chamber and inner whorls; C. septa generated from the sutures; D. unified complete shell model. — Photo: Peterman et al. 2020, PLOS ONE (CC BY 4.0)

Specimens used for the restoration: A. original nodule containing NMNS PM35490; B, C. shell sections; D. suture; E. 3D scan of the Mikasa City Museum specimen. — Photo: Peterman et al. 2020, PLOS ONE (CC BY 4.0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ancyloceratina / Family Ancyloceratidae
species.distribution: Queensland, Australia: Rolling Downs / Hughenden district, Allaru Mudstone, Blackdown Formation, Maryborough Basin.
species.diagnosis: (Genus characters) Evolute shell, with early-whorl ribbing alternating between smooth ribs and ribs with coarse blunt nodes; outer-whorl ribbing without nodes, entirely smooth; the suture and whorl-section details of A. jacki itself are not verified.
species.remarks: The type species of the genus Australiceras and the index fossil of the lower Aptian Australiceras beds of eastern Australia; it contrasts with the Aptian Ancyloceras of Europe.

images.caption: Australiceras jacki fossil exhibited at the Musée des Confluences, Lyon, from Queensland, Australia. — Photo: Vassil (Wikimedia Commons) (CC0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ancyloceratina / Superfamily Ancyloceratoidea / Family Ancyloceratidae / Subfamily Ancyloceratinae
species.distribution: France (type locality, Paris Basin), middle Volga River, Russia, Morocco.
species.diagnosis: A hook-shaped (ancylocone) heteromorph shell: composed of a spiral part, a straight part, a bent part and a recurved part; shell length up to 30–40 cm; the juvenile spiral part initially bears node-bearing ribs, with the nodes soon disappearing; the suture type of this species is not verified.
species.remarks: The type species of the type genus of the family Ancyloceratidae — i.e. the name-bearer of the entire ancyloceratid group; one of the most representative ammonite genera of the Lower Cretaceous.

images.caption: Ancyloceras matheronianum fossil exhibited at the Natural History Museum, Berlin, from Roquefort, France. — Photo: Daderot (Wikimedia Commons) (CC0)

species.classification: Order Ammonitida / Suborder Ancyloceratina / Family Nostoceratidae (position disputed; also placed in Turrilitidae or Didymoceratidae)
species.age: Late Cretaceous, late Campanian; zonal fossil of the Didymoceras stevensoni Zone
species.distribution: Pierre Shale of the Western Interior Seaway, USA: South Dakota, Wyoming, near Pueblo, Colorado, Carter County, Montana.
species.diagnosis: A shell that rises in a spiral and then ends in a loosely hooked portion; the spiral part may coil to the left or to the right; 21–30 ribs per half whorl in the spiral stage; nodes small and node-like with flat tops, as if once bearing small sharp spines; the adult body chamber comprises the last half whorl of the spiral part plus the subsequent loosely recurved whorl; suture type not verified.
species.remarks: A classic “corkscrew-plus-hook” Western Interior heteromorph and the zonal fossil of one of four successive late Campanian heteromorph zones; still-water modelling studies suggest this shell form was low-energy in lifestyle, able to hover in the water column and rotate about a vertical axis.

images.caption: Didymoceras stevensoni shell exhibited at the Houston Museum of Natural Science, from the Pierre Shale of Weston County, Wyoming, USA. — Photo: Daderot (Wikimedia Commons) (CC0)

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Small to medium-sized shell. During ontogeny the shell shape and ornament change markedly. Small specimens (under 10 mm) are discoidal, evolute to semi-evolute, with a broad rounded venter and narrow rounded flanks. The umbilicus is small, about 1/2 of the shell diameter. The whorl cross-section is reniform. Fine transverse ribs develop on the umbilical margin; each rib bifurcates into 2-3 fine transverse lines that incline slightly forward and form a shallow ventral sinus at the venter. The longitudinal striae are very weak. Each whorl bears three narrow, shallow constrictions. Slightly larger specimens (over 10 mm in diameter) are thickly discoidal and semi-involute. The body chamber is one whorl long. The venter and flanks are arched and rounded. The whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical. The umbilicus is about 1/3 of the shell diameter, with an angular umbilical margin and a low, steep umbilical wall. Nodose ribs occur on the umbilical margin. The shell surface bears reticulate ornament; the growth lines are fine and dense, and the longitudinal spiral striae are relatively coarse. The constrictions are weak or absent. External suture: the broad ventral lobe is divided by a low, broad median ventral saddle into two straight, tongue-shaped branch lobes; the lateral lobe is V-shaped; the lateral saddle is broad and rounded.

F001000284; collected at Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China. Age, locality and description follow the NIMRF record of the illustrated specimen; order and family are not verified from that source.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Liuyazi, Nanjiang County, Bazhong City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Semi-involute shell, thinly discoidal. The umbilicus is wide, about 1/3 of the shell diameter, with a sloping umbilical wall. The venter is narrow and flat, with angular ventrolateral margins. The flanks are flat, with a row of stout tubercles or spinose tubercles at mid-flank. Another row of wart-like tubercles occurs on the ventrolateral margin, more densely spaced, numbering about twice the lateral tubercles. The suture is not observed.

species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell shape and ornament of this species are similar to those of R. pachygyrum. It differs in the adult-stage characters of the described specimen: (1) the shell is thin, the venter is arched and rounded, and the whorl cross-section is nearly as high as wide; (2) the nodose ribs on the umbilical margin gradually weaken and finally disappear; (3) there are no constrictions; (4) in the external suture the ventral lobe is long, the lateral lobe is narrow and V-shaped, and the top of the first lateral saddle is narrow and rounded.

species.diagnosis: Small shell, thickly discoidal; the juvenile shell is semi-evolute and the adult shell semi- involute. The whorl section is ring-shaped. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuohoushan, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The characters of the specimen are the same as those of Berriasella oppeli described by Mazenot and Le Hégarat. They are similar to the B. oppeli described by Chao (1976), but with lower rib density and more single ribs. Suture: the features are not clear because the specimen is eroded. A broad, high ventral saddle is visible, with small ventral branch lobes, and the external saddle is divided by a small lobe into two equal parts. The first lateral lobe is well developed, long, with a broad base and a pointed tail, and symmetrical lateral branches; the second lateral lobe is shorter and inclined. The first and second lateral saddles are rather narrow. The auxiliary lobe system is simple.

The transverse ribs arise near the umbilical shoulder and end at the ventrolateral part. The ventral lobe of the external suture is unknown; the flank has one pair of lateral lobes and two pairs of umbilical lobes; the lateral lobe is slightly broad, slightly constricted in its upper part and expanded below; the first umbilical lobe is narrower and shorter than the lateral lobe; the second umbilical lobe lies on both sides of the umbilical seam; all saddles are about as wide as the lateral lobe, equal in height, with smoothly rounded tops. Owing to weathering, the serrations at the lower ends of the lateral and umbilical lobes are indistinct.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell rather small, semi-evolute and thickly discoidal. Whorl cross-section crescent- shaped, height 1/3 of width. Venter broad and rounded, flanks narrow, sloping towards the venter. Umbilicus deep and rather large, 1/2 of the shell diameter, umbilical shoulder subangular, umbilical wall steep and low. Shell surface with reticulate ornament; short ribs at the umbilical shoulder arise from the umbilical wall and branch into fan-shaped transverse striae, 3-5 in number. The transverse striae incline slightly forward and form a shallow ventral bend at the venter. The longitudinal striae are slightly weaker than the transverse striae. Constrictions are rather narrow, curving in the same direction as the transverse striae. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is broad, the median ventral saddle rather high and bottle-shaped, the ventral lobe branches slightly expanded in the middle and lower parts; the lateral lobe is V-shaped; the first lateral saddle is broad and high, with a rounded top; the second lateral saddle is slightly lower than the first and asymmetrical; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall and is shallow and funnel- shaped.

species.distribution: Penglaitan, Etoushan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell of medium size, diameter 20-45 mm, semi-involute, wheel-shaped. Whorl height greater than thickness; cross-section nearly rectangular. On the inner whorls the venter is narrow and roof-shaped; towards the front of the outer whorl the venter widens, with a low, blunt median ventral keel and bluntly angular ventrolateral shoulders. Flanks broad, with a thick, protruding longitudinal ridge on the inner flank, sloping gradually outward from the ridge and becoming slightly concave towards the outer flank. Shell surface bears curved fine transverse striae. Umbilicus rather large, about one-third of the shell diameter; umbilical shoulder slightly convex; umbilical wall of medium height and steep. Suture: ventral lobe narrow and of medium length, divided by a moderately high median saddle into two narrow, elongate ventral prongs; first lateral lobe long and broad, located on both sides of the ventrolateral ridge, its lower end bearing six denticles of unequal length; second lateral lobe longer, half as wide as the first lateral lobe, its end with two small denticles and one small projection; first lateral saddle rather narrow, slightly constricted in the middle, with rounded top; second lateral saddle wider and higher than the first, its upper part narrowing into a narrow arch, inclined slightly towards the umbilicus; three narrow, short small lobes on the umbilical shoulder and umbilical wall.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Several flattened specimens. Shell large, semi-evolute, discoidal, whorls coiled elliptically. Venter arched and rounded; flanks slightly convex, most convex near the umbilical shoulder, sloping gradually and slowly towards the venter from there. Umbilicus shallow, umbilical width about one-third of the shell diameter; umbilical shoulder subangular; umbilical wall low and rather steep. Body chamber extends for half a whorl. On the inner whorls the flanks bear nodes, which gradually enlarge as the whorls grow; from the posterior part of the outer whorl the nodes progressively become thicker and longer; towards the middle they become short, stout transverse ribs; towards the front the transverse ribs become still thicker, broad at the base and pointed at the top, wedge- shaped, more closely spaced, and markedly inclined forward on the ventrolateral flank. Transverse ribs start from the umbilical wall and disappear at the ventrolateral flank. External suture: ventral lobe bipartite; lateral lobe narrow and long, constricted above, inflated in the middle, pointed at the end, with 7-8 small denticles; umbilical lobe two- thirds the length of the lateral lobe, V-shaped, its end with 4-5 serrations; first lateral saddle broad, its top arched and rounded, slightly constricted in the middle; second lateral saddle lower than the first lateral saddle, with rounded top.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Majiashan, Chaohu City, Anhui Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell small, semi-evolute, discoidal. Whorls deeply embracing; cross-section elongate- elliptical. Venter narrow and rounded, flanks somewhat flattened; umbilicus of medium width and depth. The surfaces of the venter and ventrolateral parts bear uniform fine longitudinal lirae and indistinct fold-like wrinkles. These wrinkles start outside the umbilical shoulder and disappear before reaching the venter. The inner part of the flanks has no longitudinal lirae, only fold wrinkles. Suture of a very distinctive shape, composed of one short, broad ventral lobe and two short, broad lateral lobes. The ventral lobe is divided by a very broad median saddle into two short, simple ventral prongs. The lower end of the first lateral lobe bears 8-10 prominent denticles arranged in an arc. The second lateral lobe is very short, located outside the umbilical shoulder, its lower end with only a few denticles. The auxiliary suture series is very short, restricted to the umbilical wall.

species.diagnosis: Shell nearly evolute, discoidal. Venter with a distinct median ventral keel. Flanks slightly convex. Umbilicus rather shallow, of medium width. Inner whorls with prominent nodes on the flanks. The penultimate whorl bears moderately coarse short ribs and ventrolateral nodes. On the posterior part of the outer whorl, a rather long and slightly curved transverse rib starts from the umbilical shoulder, becomes coarser outwards, and suddenly weakens near the ventrolateral shoulder, immediately followed by a coarser ventrolateral node; towards the front of the outer whorl the transverse ribs become distinctly weaker and denser, interspersed with very fine, slightly curved ribbing, and the corresponding ventrolateral nodes are particularly small; these ribs extend into the roof- shaped venter, forming chevron-shaped ornament. The ventrolateral shoulder on the front part of the outer whorl is raised and ridge-like. Suture: lateral lobe long, constricted above and slightly inflated below, its lower end with nine denticles; first umbilical lobe rather short, narrowing downwards, its lower end with three coarse denticles; second umbilical lobe with nine denticles; dorsal lobe very narrow and bifid.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium-sized, semi-evolute, discoidal, comprising about two whorls. Venter arched and rounded; flanks slightly convex, most convex at the inner middle flank. Umbilicus shallow, umbilical width slightly less than one-third of the shell diameter; umbilical wall low and sloping, umbilical shoulder fairly rounded. The inner whorls bear fine rib-like nodes on the flanks; as the whorls grow, the rib-like nodes become thicker and larger, becoming short, stout transverse ribs in the middle and posterior part of the outer whorl, and lengthening towards the anterior part, with decreasing rib spacing. The transverse ribs all arise from the umbilical shoulder, incline slightly backwards, thicken near the ventrolateral shoulder, incline forwards, and end at the ventrolateral flank. External suture: ventral lobe bipartite, the ventral lobe narrowed and pointed; lateral lobe long, with a small tooth at its lower end; first umbilical lobe narrow, half the length of the lateral lobe, toothed at its end; second umbilical lobe located on both sides of the umbilical line, shallow 'V'-shaped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. YF0637, resource no. F001005393; collected at Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Province, China. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell semi-evolute, discoidal. Whorl height increases fairly rapidly; outer whorl height greater than thickness, maximum thickness at the umbilical shoulder. Whorl cross-section slightly semi-elliptical, flanks flattened. Venter narrow, arched and rounded. Flanks slightly arched, converging slightly towards the venter. Umbilical width about one-third of the shell diameter; umbilical shoulder well rounded. Inner whorls bear nodose ribs on the flanks; the penultimate whorl bears short, stout, radial transverse ribs; on the outer whorl these become fine, dense ribbing, the ribs arising from the umbilical shoulder, ending at the ventrolateral flank and curving slightly forwards. External suture: ventral lobe fairly wide and short; ventral branch lobe shows no small teeth, possibly because the specimen is excessively corroded; lateral lobe the longest, constricted in its upper part, with 5-6 small teeth at its lower end; first umbilical lobe short, with 3-4 small teeth at its lower end. Second lateral saddle wide and low.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell small, flatly discoidal; in the juvenile stage the shell is semi-evolute, in the adult stage semi-involute, comprising about 7 whorls. Whorl cross-section semicircular to rounded-triangular, height greater than width. Venter arched and rounded. Flanks fairly wide, inclining slightly towards the venter; maximum thickness at the umbilical shoulder. Umbilicus medium-sized, about one-third of the shell diameter; umbilical wall low, inclining slightly inwards; umbilical shoulder well rounded. Shell surface ornamented with fine transverse striae, arising from the umbilical shoulder, increasing by intercalation at the middle flank, and bending backwards at the ventrolateral shoulder to form a ventral bend. On the flanks of the whorls, a shallow constriction groove occurs every 3-4 mm, running in the same direction as the transverse striae. External suture: ventral lobe fairly wide, divided into two branches by a moderately high, fairly wide median saddle; ventral branch lobe pointed tongue-shaped, siphonal lobe short tongue-shaped; lateral lobe wide, 'V'-shaped, only half the length of the ventral lobe, slightly swollen in the middle; umbilical lobe located on the umbilical wall, shallow and rounded; first lateral saddle high, its top constricted and arched-rounded. Septa dense, one suture line occurring every 1 mm.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. X0154-03, resource no. F001000296; collected at Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuohoushan, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell thickly discoidal, whorl thickness slightly greater than height. Venter flat, with a wide, smooth band. Shell surface ornamented with strong ribs running radially and inclining slightly forwards; the ribs arise from the umbilical shoulder, becoming low, long nodes at the middle of the flanks or near the umbilical shoulder, then dividing into two branch ribs, the ribs slightly arched and inclining forwards. A few single ribs are also intercalated; all ribs end at the sides of the smooth ventral band and swell there, forming leaf-like long nodes. Suture: ventral saddle serrated; ventral branch lobe splits into fine branches and reaches about the same height as the first lateral lobe. The external saddle is divided by a slender small lobe into two equal parts. The first lateral lobe is stout and long, with a slender tail branch and lateral branches on both sides, the outer lateral branch more developed than the inner. The first lateral saddle is narrower and smaller than the external saddle.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Etoushan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: All are phragmocone parts. Shell medium-sized, shell diameter 27-35 mm, nearly involute, thinly discoidal. Whorl height greater than thickness. Venter fairly narrow, with a median ventral keel; ventrolateral shoulder rounded. Flanks fairly wide and flat, ornamented with 4 evenly distributed longitudinal spiral ridges; the ridges are low and narrow, most developed on the outer whorl, and, as seen from the internal mould, lie on both sides of the saddles. As the shell material is not preserved, other ornament is unknown. Umbilicus shallow and small, about 1/9-1/8 of the shell diameter; umbilical shoulder subangular, umbilical wall low and steep. Septa very closely spaced; the outer whorl bears 21 septa, and the lobe of one suture line often meets the saddle of the next suture line. Suture: ventral lobe wide and short, divided by a moderately high median saddle into 2 ventral branch lobes; the ventral branch lobes lie at the ventrolateral shoulder, slightly swollen in the middle, with pointed ends; first lateral saddle moderately high, its top slightly constricted and inclining slightly towards the venter; first lateral lobe twice as long as the ventral lobe, with 6-7 teeth of varying thickness at its end; second lateral saddle higher than the first lateral saddle, its top wide and rounded; second lateral lobe fairly short and narrow, with 5 serrations in its lower part; the auxiliary lobe system is developed with 2 small lobes, one of which is bipartite at its end.

species.distribution: Penglaitan, Etoushan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell of varying size, shell diameter 20-35 mm, nearly involute, thinly discoidal. Venter narrow, with a median ventral keel; ventrolateral shoulder arched and rounded. Flanks fairly wide; inner flank slightly concave, middle flank slightly convex, outer flank inclining towards the venter. Shell surface ornamented with fine, sickle-shaped growth lines, bending slightly forwards at the venter. The posterior part of the outer whorl bears forward-projecting transverse ribs. The flanks of the phragmocone bear 2 low, narrow longitudinal spiral ridges at the middle flank, which are indistinct on the body chamber. Umbilicus small, about 1/6 of the shell diameter; umbilical wall low and steep. Suture: ventral lobe fairly long, ventral branch lobe narrow and pointed; first lateral saddle wide and rounded; first lateral lobe long, about as wide as the lateral saddle, with 6 teeth of varying length at its lower end; second lateral saddle high, its top arched and rounded, inclining slightly towards the umbilicus; second lateral lobe short, with 7 fairly uniform small teeth at its end; the auxiliary lobe system is not very well developed.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell fairly large, semi-evolute, discoidal, comprising about four whorls; the inner whorls increase slowly in height, the outer whorl increasing markedly. Venter of unknown form, apparently arched and rounded; flanks slightly convex, most convex at the inner middle flank, converging gradually towards the venter from there. Umbilicus shallow, about one- third of the shell diameter; umbilical wall low and sloping, umbilical shoulder well rounded. Body chamber more than half a whorl in length. The inner whorls bear small, transverse nodes on the flanks; the second and following whorls bear fairly stout longitudinal nodes on the flanks, becoming short, stout T-shaped nodes on the posterior part of the outer whorl. Straight nodose ribs begin in the middle of the outer whorl, becoming stout transverse ribs towards the anterior part, bending forwards at the ventrolateral shoulder. The transverse ribs arise from the umbilical wall and end at the ventrolateral flank. Ventrolateral flank well rounded. Flanks narrow and convex. Umbilicus fairly deep, umbilical width slightly less than two-fifths of the shell diameter, umbilical shoulder rounded, umbilical wall fairly high and steep. Body chamber very long, about three- quarters of the outer whorl. External suture: lateral lobe fairly long, slightly constricted in its upper part, with 8-9 stout teeth at its lower end; first umbilical lobe short, with 7-8 small teeth at its lower end. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Zhuobeixigou, east of Gyantse County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell semi-evolute, discoidal, with a fairly large umbilicus; flanks slightly convex, venter flat with a median ventral groove. Whorl cross-section elliptical. Surface bears distinct transverse ribs arising from umbilical tubercles and bifurcating; mid-flanks bear spinose mid-lateral tubercles, from which the ribs branch again and curve slightly forward. Between the tubercles on both sides there are 1-3 single or paired ribs without spinose tubercles. On the inner whorls the umbilical tubercles are indistinct while the mid-lateral tubercles are developed; on the outer whorl the umbilical tubercles are prominent and the mid-lateral tubercles disappear or are only slightly swollen. The rib ends swell into small nodes and terminate on the venter as ventrolateral tubercles. Suture: first lateral lobe long and broad, digitate; saddles divided in a foliate manner.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Douling Village Coal Mine and Salt Lake, Baifang Town, Changning City, Hengyang City, Hunan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell semi-involute, thickly discoidal, umbilicus small, u/b ratio about 0.23. Outer whorl bears a distinct ventral keel, flanks slightly arched, cross-section subtriangular; venter bears 18-20 longitudinal lirae. Inner whorls have a rounded venter, keel indistinct, longitudinal lirae present over the whole venter and flanks. Near the ventrolateral shoulders on both sides there are 3 prominent longitudinal lirae, more widely spaced; with these as a boundary, the longitudinal lirae on the inner flanks gradually disappear towards adulthood. Inner whorls show distinct growth lines and constrictions, which form a rounded, deep ventral sinus on the venter. Growth lines commonly intersect the longitudinal lirae forming a reticulate pattern. Umbilical shoulder rounded, umbilical wall fairly high and steep. Suture: ventral lobe broad; in early development its sides are nearly straight and the ventral branches asymmetrical; later the sides bend slightly and the ventral branches become fairly symmetrical and lanceolate; lateral lobe nearly inverted- bell-shaped; median and external saddles both fairly wide.

species.diagnosis: Shell fairly large, evolute, discoidal; outer whorl cross-section semi-elliptical, height greater than thickness. Venter smooth, fairly narrow, evenly rounded. Ventrolateral parts rounded, flanks slightly convex. Umbilicus shallow, umbilical width almost half the shell diameter, umbilical shoulder fairly rounded, umbilical wall low and steep. Body chamber more than half a whorl long. Inner whorls narrow on the flanks, with small nodose ribs; as the whorl grows the ribs gradually thicken, becoming very coarse radial transverse ribs by the penultimate whorl; the ribs weaken outward from the umbilical shoulder and disappear on the ventrolateral parts; on the outermost whorl they become fine transverse ribs inclined forward, extending backward obliquely from the umbilical seam, turning forward at the middle of the umbilical wall and gradually thickening, becoming straight and coarse on the inner flank, then weakening and finally disappearing on the ventrolateral parts, curving slightly forward. Suture: ventral lobe broad and short; lateral lobe long, its sides nearly parallel, lower end with 7-8 denticles; first umbilical lobe narrow and short, lower end with 3-4 denticles. Median saddle broad and low; external and lateral saddles with nearly parallel sides, their widths and heights nearly equal.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell shape and ornament change markedly during ontogeny. Small to medium specimens (shell diameter under 30 mm) are flatly discoidal, semi-involute. Whorl cross- section transversely kidney-shaped. Venter evenly rounded, flanks fairly narrow, inclined towards the venter. Umbilicus moderately large, the transverse ribs on the umbilical shoulder fine and short. Growth lines distinct, longitudinal lines weak. Three constrictions per whorl. Large shells (30-80 mm) are flatly cake-shaped, semi-involute. Whorl cross- section rounded-triangular. Venter narrowly rounded. Flanks fairly broad. Greatest thickness at the umbilical shoulder. Umbilicus small, its width 1/4 of the shell diameter, umbilical shoulder angular, umbilical wall fairly high and steep. Ribs on the umbilical shoulder gradually disappear as the shell grows; the shell is ornamented with wavy, fine longitudinal and transverse lirae, the transverse lirae forming a broad, deep ventral sinus on the venter. Constrictions disappear on the adult shell. External suture: ventral lobe broad, median saddle fairly broad, its height half that of the ventral lobe; in juveniles the lateral lobe is inverted-helmet-shaped, its outer side slightly expanded; in adults the lateral lobe is a narrow 'V' shape; first lateral saddle broad, its top fairly rounded; second lateral saddle broad, rounded and asymmetrical; umbilical lobe at the umbilical shoulder, funnel-shaped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. X0153-13, resource no. F001000293; collected at Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell diameter 22-42 mm, involute, subspherical or flatly spherical. Whorl cross-section crescentic or slightly triangular. In juveniles the venter is broadly rounded, becoming narrow and arched as the whorl grows. Flanks fairly convex; shell surface bears fine transverse ribs and 4 constrictions dividing the whorl into four quadrants. Ribs arise at the umbilical shoulder, inclined slightly forward, beginning to bifurcate on the inner flanks, with intercalated ribs between the bifurcating ribs. The first few short ribs become parabolic, bending backward on the outer part and crossing the venter. Umbilicus small and deep, umbilical shoulder subangular, umbilical wall slightly steep. In juveniles the suture is fairly completely preserved, subammonitic, with 6-7 lobes; the top of the external saddle bears a small divided leaflet, the other saddles are entire, the lateral lobes digitate, the umbilical lobe simple. Two larger specimens have nine lobes, with part of the suture preserved.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: north of Jurila, Qiongguo Township, Zhongba County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium to fairly large, involute, thickly discoidal. Venter evenly rounded, flanks gently convex, ventrolateral parts broadly rounded, whorl cross-section nearly horseshoe- shaped, greatest shell width at the umbilical shoulder. During ontogeny, whorl height increases slightly faster than width. Ornament weak, shell surface nearly smooth. Umbilicus small and deep, umbilical shoulder bluntly rounded, umbilical wall steep. Subammonitic suture; lobes of the internal and external sutures similar in shape, columnar, strongly divided on both sides. Ventral lobe broad and deep, garlic-bulb- shaped, divided by a tall columnar median saddle into 2 broad, deep, digitately divided ventral branches. Median saddle height nearly 4/5 of the external saddle, its width close to that of the lower part of the ventral branches. External saddle slightly inclined towards the venter, its top divided, with 11 lobes on each side.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small and discoidal. The two flanks are flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, the convexity being greater in the body chamber than on the inner whorls, but gradually converging towards the venter. The whorl cross-section is elongate subquadrate. On the inner whorls the shell surface bears fine, dense, radiate, slightly curved transverse ribs; on the body chamber the ribs become sparser and straighter. The intercostal grooves are uniform; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate at one-third of the way out to the flanks. Single ribs are only occasionally inserted in the phragmocone; all ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, slightly swollen, but without forming tubercles.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuohoushan, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, evolute and thinly discoidal. The outermost whorl increases in height rather rapidly, embracing one-quarter of the preceding whorl. The umbilicus is rather small, less than one-third of the diameter, with a rather steep umbilical wall and an indistinct umbilical margin. The two flanks are flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, and the whorl cross-section is rectangular. The venter is narrow and flat, with a shallow median ventral groove. The shell surface bears strong transverse ribs slanting forward. The ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate at one-third of the way out to the flanks, but in some specimens the bifurcation point lies slightly closer to the mid-flanks. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove and thicken, forming projections or tubercles. The projections and tubercles occur in a regular alternating pattern. The tubercles are mostly formed where a primary rib meets a secondary rib, but some are formed where an anterior rib meets a posterior rib, and occasionally a single thickened rib forms a tubercle. The regular arrangement of the tubercles is the most distinctive feature of this species.

The flanks are rather wide; the mid-flanks and the outer flanks are slightly convex, forming 2 low, wide longitudinal spiral ridges; on the inner flanks of the anterior part of the outer whorl there are faint radiate fine transverse ribs. The umbilicus is shallow and small, about 1/7 of the shell diameter, the umbilical margin flat and subangular, the umbilical wall low and steep. The suture: the ventral lobe is rather short and wide, divided by a low, wide, flat median saddle into 2 prongs; the ventral prongs are narrow and pointed; the first lateral saddle is short, slanting slightly towards the venter, with a rounded saddle top; the first lateral lobe is about as wide as the first lateral saddle, narrowing gradually from top to bottom, with 7 denticles of unequal length at its end; the second lateral saddle is wide and high, the top arched and rounded, slanting slightly towards the umbilicus; the second lateral lobe is short and narrow, slightly swollen in the middle on the ventral side, narrowing below, with 3 denticles of equal size at its end; the auxiliary series is developed, differentiating into 4 narrow, pointed small lobes.

species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium-sized to large, evolute, discoidal. The outer whorl is higher than thick, with maximum thickness at the umbilical margin; whorl cross-section slightly elliptical, flanks compressed. Venter narrowly arched. Flanks rather flat, converging toward the venter; ventrolateral region rounded. Umbilicus large, about 1/2 of the shell diameter; umbilical margin rounded, umbilical wall low. Inner whorls bear nodes on the flanks; by the penultimate whorl the flanks develop rather coarse radial transverse ribs with wide spacing; on the outermost whorl the ornament becomes finer and weaker, changing to fine dense striae that start at the umbilical margin, end at the ventrolateral region, and incline slightly forward. External suture: the ventral lobe is rather narrow and long; the lateral lobe is long, slightly constricted in the middle-upper part and slightly expanded in the lower part, with 8 denticulations at its lower end; the first umbilical lobe bears 5-6 denticulations at its lower end. The median ventral saddle is high and narrow, with nearly parallel sides; the lateral saddle is as wide as the external saddle but slightly lower.
