species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium-sized, evolute, thickly discoidal. Whorls increase evenly in size; involution 1/3. Umbilicus large; umbilical wall steeply inclined; umbilical margin indistinct. Whorl thickness slightly greater than height; venter arched, with a broad shallow median ventral groove. Whorl cross-section subcircular. Shell surface ornamented with strong radial transverse ribs; ribs start at the umbilical margin and become distinct angular nodes toward the mid-flank. The nodes are nodose or spine-like, each node formed by the junction of two branch ribs, or by the junction of a main rib and a branch rib. Between two nodes there is usually one intercalated rib, and in a few cases two branch ribs are intercalated between two nodes. Suture: ventral saddle broad and high; ventral prongs narrow and small, but at the same height as the first lateral lobe. External saddle broad and high, divided by a small lobe into two equal parts. First lateral lobe coarse and long, with three large lateral branches, the terminal branch long and pointed; second lateral lobe narrow and small, also with asymmetrical lateral branches. First lateral saddle narrower than the external saddle, also divided by a small lobe.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, semi-evolute and flattened discoidal. The flanks are flattened and slightly convex. The umbilicus is of moderate size, about 1/3 of the shell diameter, with a low, gently sloping umbilical wall. The inner whorls bear fine ribbing on the flanks; the posterior part of the outer whorl bears short, fine transverse ribs, which become slightly forward-inclined transverse ribs toward the front, and become dense and fine again near the aperture. The ribs start from the umbilical margin, gradually becoming coarser outward, becoming coarsest at the ventrolateral margin where they bend forward, then rapidly disappearing. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is bifid; the lateral lobe is long, with sides almost parallel, bearing 5-6 fine denticles at its lower end; the first umbilical lobe is narrow, about 1/2 as long as the lateral lobe, bearing 3-4 serrations at its lower end; the first lateral saddle is slightly higher than the second lateral saddle and the umbilical saddle, with a broad, rounded top.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, comprising 3-4 whorls, nearly evolute and discoidal. The inner whorls grow at a uniform rate, while the outer whorl increases rapidly in height. The shape of the venter is unknown. The flanks are flat, the umbilicus shallow, slightly less than 1/3 of the shell diameter in width, with a rounded umbilical margin and a low umbilical wall. The inner whorls bear fine, dense transverse ribs on the flanks; on the anterior part of the penultimate whorl the transverse ribs end at the ventrolateral margin as small tubercles; as the whorls grow, the transverse ribs gradually become coarser, becoming stout and slightly forward-inclined in the middle to anterior part of the outer whorl, thinning at the outer-middle part of the flanks and then becoming coarse, large, rounded tubercles. On the inner whorls the transverse ribs start from the umbilical margin and end at the ventrolateral margin, while on the outer whorl the ribs start from outside the umbilical seam and disappear at the ventrolateral margin. The ventral lobe of the external suture is not exposed. The lateral lobe is rather long, slightly constricted in its upper part, with several denticles at its lower end; the umbilical lobe is slightly shorter, with sides almost parallel, bearing 6-7 serrations at its lower end; the first lateral saddle is high, and the second lateral saddle and the umbilical saddle are both lower than the first lateral saddle, with broad, rounded tops.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium-sized, evolute, discoidal. Body chamber about half a whorl long, cross- section rectangular, flanks compressed, greatest thickness at the swelling in the middle of the flank. The venter of the posterior part of the outer whorl is steeply roof-shaped, with a distinct median ventral keel; flanks flat; ventrolateral margin subangular, becoming gradually flatter toward the aperture on the ventral side, and flat at the very front; at the same time the part of the flank near the ventrolateral margin gradually becomes concave, and the ventrolateral margin gradually becomes a prominent sharp keel. Umbilical margin rounded, umbilical wall low and steep, umbilicus about 1/3 of the shell diameter or slightly more. On the posterior part of the penultimate whorl, the flanks bear radial ribs; toward the front, the ribs incline forward and terminate at the ventrolateral margin in small nodes. On the posterior part of the outer whorl the ribs are rather coarse and curved, arising from the umbilical seam, bending distinctly backward near the umbilical margin, bending slightly forward in the middle of the flank, bending backward again near the ventrolateral margin, and forming rather coarse nodes at the ventrolateral margin, continuing obliquely forward into the venter to form an atypical chevron ornament. From the posterior to the anterior part of the body chamber, the ribs on the flanks gradually become finer and denser; the ventrolateral nodes gradually become smaller until they disappear, and the chevron ornament on the venter becomes increasingly distinct. Between the ribs of the outer whorl there are also very fine growth lines, running in the same direction as the ribs and likewise forming a chevron pattern on the venter. External suture: ventral lobe rather short, with two branches; lateral lobe broad and long, narrowing slightly downward, with 5-6 coarse denticles at the lower end; first umbilical lobe rather short and tongue-shaped, with 5 denticles at the lower end. External saddle and lateral saddle rather narrow; umbilical saddle broadest.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell medium-sized, semi-evolute, discoidal, comprising about four whorls. Shape of the venter unclear, apparently arched and rounded; flanks slightly convex, most convex at the middle-inner flank. Umbilicus shallow, umbilical width slightly less than 1/3 of the shell diameter; umbilical wall low and sloping, umbilical margin rather rounded. The flanks of the inner whorls are ornamented with fine rib-like nodes; as the whorls grow the rib-like nodes become coarser and larger, becoming short coarse transverse ribs on the middle- posterior part of the outer whorl, and longer transverse ribs toward the front, with smaller rib spacing. All transverse ribs arise from the umbilical margin, incline slightly backward, become coarser near the ventrolateral margin, incline forward, and terminate at the ventrolateral part. External suture: ventral lobe bipartite, becoming narrow and pointed; lateral lobe long, with 8-9 small denticles at the lower end; first umbilical lobe narrow, half the length of the lateral lobe, with 3-4 denticles at the end; second umbilical lobe located on both sides of the umbilical seam, shallowly V-shaped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. X0202-02, resource no. F001000537; collected at Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. Age, locality and description follow the NIMRF record of the illustrated specimen; order and family are not verified from that source.

species.diagnosis: Shell evolute, discoidal, umbilicus large, umbilical margin arched and rounded, umbilical wall steep and sloping. Flanks narrow and convex, venter broad and rounded. Whorl thickness greater than height, thickest near the umbilical nodes, cross-section elliptical. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: The paratype is a juvenile shell. The adult shell is medium-sized, semi-evolute, discoidal. Whorls increase slowly and evenly; cross-section slightly semi-elliptical, flanks slightly compressed, greatest thickness at the umbilical margin. Venter smooth, narrowly arched and rounded. The flanks of the inner whorls are rather arched; toward the outer whorl the flanks become flatter and converge toward the venter. Umbilicus moderately wide, umbilical width about 1/3 of the shell diameter, umbilical margin rounded. The flanks of the inner whorls bear short coarse nodose ribs; from about the third whorl onward these become radial transverse ribs, arising from the umbilical margin, becoming slightly coarser in the middle of the flank and then weakening, terminating at the ventrolateral part. The holotype is incomplete, and the ornament on the flank of the outermost part of the shell could not be seen, but other specimens show that the flank corresponding to that part bears fine dense radial striae. External suture: lateral lobe rather long, sides nearly parallel, with 6-7 denticles at the lower end; first umbilical lobe narrow and rather long, narrowing distinctly downward, with 3-4 denticles at the lower end. Lateral saddle and external saddle equal in height.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. X0203-05, resource no. F001000327; collected at Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China. species.distribution: Guojiashan, Qinyu Township, Dangchang County, Gansu Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell rather small, flat discoidal, semi-evolute; umbilicus rather deep, umbilical wall steep. Venter narrow and rounded, with a weak ventral keel. The outer whorl embraces about 1/2 of the inner whorl, and the inner whorl indents the outer whorl by about 1/3. The body chamber is rather flat, gradually forming an arc toward the apical side. Ventrolateral shoulder indistinct. Whorl height slightly greater than width; in some specimens height and width are nearly equal; cross-section elliptical. The flanks bear ribs, stronger near the umbilicus, with a row of small tubercles on the umbilical margin; the ribs extend from the umbilical margin toward the venter and disappear in the middle of the flank. The first few whorls bear no ornament.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is large and thick-discoidal. The umbilical wall is steep and inclined; the umbilical margin is rather rounded but indistinct. The two flanks are arched and rounded, converging rather rapidly near the venter. The greatest thickness of the whorl lies at the middle of the flanks, and the cross-section is subquadrate and rounded, with a slightly concave venter bearing a broad smooth band. The shell surface bears coarse radial ribs that arise at the umbilical margin and extend outward, becoming thicker toward the flanks near the umbilical margin and forming long, nodose ribs. Suture: the median ventral saddle is narrow and high, serrated. The ventral branches are narrow and pointed, lying at the same position as the first lateral lobe; the external saddle is divided by a slender small lobe into equal parts. The first lateral lobe has a broad main branch and well-developed side branches; the side branch near the umbilical margin is somewhat longer than the one near the venter; the terminal branch is pointed and long.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, evolute and thick-discoidal. The outer whorl grows rapidly, with an involution of one quarter. The cross-section is subquadrate and rounded. The venter is narrow and flat, with a broad, shallow smooth band. The shell surface bears delicate, rather dense transverse ribs extending obliquely forward; the ribs are carinate, arising at the umbilical margin and extending outward, swelling at one-third of the flank to form long, carinate projections; from there the main ribs bifurcate outward, with a few single ribs intercalated; the main and branch ribs all extend obliquely forward and are interrupted and thickened at the ventrolateral margin, but without forming nodes. On the inner whorls the ribs bifurcate at the middle of the flanks, evenly distributed and carinate. Suture: the ventral saddle is high, its top divided into two parts by a small groove; the ventral branches are narrow, slightly higher than the ends of the first lateral lobe. The external saddle is broad and high, divided by a slender small lobe into equal parts; the first lateral lobe is broad and long, trifurcating at its base, with a slender, long terminal branch; the first lateral saddle is narrower than the external saddle and divided by two small lobes. The second lateral lobe is short and small.

F003005199; collected at Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China. species.diagnosis: The specimen is 70 mm long, 70 mm wide and 10 mm high, grey and brown in colour. On it is a fossil of Clypeoceras lenticulare, about 15 mm long. The taxonomic position of Clypeoceras lenticulare is: Animalia, Mollusca, Ammonoidea. In this group the shell is involute, with discoidal whorls, a distinct umbilical margin, a high, steep umbilical wall and a narrow, small umbilicus. The shell surface is smooth. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Dagangping Village, Yangchun City, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is rather large, nearly involute and thick-discoidal, with an arched, rounded venter, broad rounded ventrolateral parts and gently convex flanks; the greatest shell width is at the umbilical margin; the body chamber is nearly one whorl long; in the early whorls the height is greater than the width, becoming slightly less than the width near the aperture. The outer whorl encloses the inner whorl as far as the umbilical margin, and the inner whorl is embedded to 1/4 of the height of the outer whorl; the whorl cross-section is nearly saddle-shaped or semi-ovoid. The ornament is weak. The venter and ventrolateral parts bear rather distinct longitudinal spiral lines, weaker on the flanks; growth lines are faintly visible, beginning at the umbilical seam and radiating outward, bending slightly backward on the flanks, bulging forward at the ventrolateral parts, with a distinct ventral sinus. The early whorls bear umbilical nodes. The suture is of the Gastrioceras type; the ventral lobe is bipartite, broad and basin-shaped; the ventral branches are partly poorly preserved; the lateral lobe is distinctly narrower than the ventral lobe, slightly asymmetric and inverted bell-shaped; the umbilical lobe is broad and shallow, its base near the middle of the umbilical wall; the external saddle is high and broad, saddle-shaped; the lateral saddle is low, asymmetric and broadly arched.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: south side of Shiqiantan, Qitai County, Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, discoidal and evolute, with 9-10 whorls; the inner 6 whorls are triangularly coiled, gradually becoming circularly coiled in the outer 3 whorls. The whorl height is less than the whorl thickness, and the whorl cross-section is nearly semicircular. The umbilicus is large and deep; the umbilical margin bears moderately coarse, short transverse ribs. The shell surface bears a reticulate ornament of interwoven transverse and longitudinal lines. In the suture drawn on the penultimate whorl, the ventral lobe is rather broad, divided by a rather high median saddle into two medium-sized ventral branches; the lateral lobe is slightly shorter than the ventral lobe, of medium width and inverted bell-shaped; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall, broad and shallow, with an incipient lobe still present on the umbilical wall. The suture drawn on the outer whorl (h = 13 mm, w = 17.5 mm) shows that with growth of the shell the lower ends of both the ventral branches and the lateral lobe become pointed; the external saddle is rather high and broadly rounded; the lateral saddle is lower, with a top that is not broad, asymmetric and inclined slightly toward the venter.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Changjianggou, Shangsi Township, Jiange County, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Fairly large shell, nearly evolute, discoidal; the outer whorl grows rapidly, the body chamber reaching 2/3 of a whorl in length. The flanks slope strongly inward in the juvenile stage and gradually become flat in the adult stage; the flanks of the penultimate whorl rise above the other whorls; the umbilicus is fairly wide, about 1/3 of the shell diameter; the umbilical margin is indistinct. In the juvenile stage the flanks bear sparse, short, coarse transverse ribs, which arise at the umbilical seam and become gradually coarser outward, forming coarse nodes at the ventrolateral margin; on the penultimate whorl the ventrolateral nodes are the most robust, tending to be longitudinal; on the posterior part of the final whorl the transverse ribs gradually become finer and the ventrolateral nodes correspondingly smaller; towards the middle and anterior parts of the final whorl the transverse ribs become fine and dense, becoming rib-like striae, and the ventrolateral nodes become smaller still, until they disappear. In the external suture the ventral lobe is fairly short and bifid, its branches unforked; the lateral lobe is 1.3 times as long as the ventral lobe, constricted at the lower end, with 6-7 denticles at the tip; the umbilical lobe is nearly V-shaped, slightly shorter than the lateral lobe, with 4-5 denticles at the tip; the tops of the saddles are all smoothly rounded.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Changjianggou, Shangsi Township, Jiange County, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Fairly large shell, evolute, discoidal, the body chamber reaching half a whorl in length. The whorl cross-section is rectangular, the flanks flattened; the greatest thickness lies at 1/3 of the distance from the umbilical margin to the ventrolateral margin, the thickness- to-height ratio being 4:5. From the juvenile to the adult stage, the whorl height increases rapidly, the whorl cross-section changing from inverted-trapezoidal to rectangular; the venter changes from roof-shaped to flat or even slightly depressed; the ventrolateral margin changes gradually from subangular to a raised, keeled form; the flanks change from strongly inward-sloping to gradually flat, the part near the umbilical margin becoming raised and the part near the ventrolateral margin depressed. The umbilicus is fairly deep, about 2/5 of the shell diameter in width; the umbilical margin is indistinct. In the juvenile stage the flanks bear sparse, coarse, short transverse ribs, which arise at the umbilical seam and rapidly become coarser outward, forming robust nodes at the ventrolateral margin; as the whorl grows, the transverse ribs become finer and longer and the ventrolateral nodes correspondingly smaller; in the adult stage the transverse ribs become fine and dense, becoming rib-like striae, and the ventrolateral nodes become smaller still, until they disappear; at the same time, fine, weak chevron ornament appears on the venter, formed by the rib-like striae of the flanks extending onto the venter. In the external suture the ventral lobe is fairly short and bifid, with only one ventral branch forked at its lower end; the lateral lobe is fairly long, with 6-7 denticles at the lower end; the umbilical lobe is short, nearly parallel-sided, with 6-7 denticles at the lower end; the lateral saddle is slightly wider than the external saddle.

The venter is narrowly arched in the juvenile stage and nearly keeled in the adult stage. The two flanks are nearly parallel; the shell surface bears weak growth lines. The umbilicus is large, the umbilical diameter slightly more than 1/2 of the shell diameter; the umbilical wall is low and inclined, the umbilical margin well rounded. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is constricted at the upper part and slightly expanded at the middle; the median ventral lobe is long and pointed, the ventral branches short and blunt; the lateral lobe is nearly as wide as the ventral lobe, but situated higher, its tip slightly rounded and shallowly bifid in an asymmetrical way; the umbilical lobe near the lateral lobe is slightly inclined towards the umbilicus, rounded and slightly expanded at the lower end, while the remaining umbilical lobes are short and pointed; the tops of the saddles are all smoothly rounded; the first lateral saddle is low, and the second lateral saddle is far higher and wider than the other saddles.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Etoushan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Two specimens. The shell is small, 20-25 mm in shell diameter, nearly involute, thinly discoidal. The whorl height exceeds the thickness, the cross-section spear-shaped. The venter is narrow, with a weak median ventral keel at the middle of the venter; the ventrolateral margin is subangular. The flanks are of medium width, sloping slightly towards the venter, slightly raised towards the middle and inner side. The greatest thickness lies at the umbilical margin; the outer whorl bears 3-4 weak longitudinal keels on the shell surface. Near the umbilical margin there are fine transverse ribs, the ribs extending slightly backwards. The umbilicus is shallow and small, about 1/7.5 of the shell diameter in width; the umbilical margin is subangular, the umbilical wall low and steep. In the suture, the ventral lobe is fairly wide, divided into two branches by a low median saddle; the ventral branches are narrow and pointed, with a long pointed projection at the tip, lying at the ventrolateral margin. The first lateral saddle is of medium height, its top constricted and dome-shaped; the first lateral lobe is wide and long, slightly constricted at the lower part, with 7-8 denticles of varying thickness and length at the tip; the second lateral saddle is narrow, its top narrowing and inclined slightly towards the umbilicus; the second lateral lobe is 2/3 as wide as the first lateral lobe, with 4-5 denticles at the tip; the auxiliary lobe system is fairly well developed, some of the small lobes being bifid at the lower end.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Etoushan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: All are phragmocone parts. The shell is of medium size, 27-35 mm in shell diameter, nearly involute, thinly discoidal. The whorl height exceeds the thickness. The venter is fairly narrow, with a median ventral keel; the ventrolateral margin is rounded. The flanks are fairly wide and flat, bearing four evenly distributed longitudinal spiral keels, which are low and narrow and best developed on the outer whorl; on the internal mould the keels lie on either side of the saddles and lobes. As the shell is not preserved, other ornament is unknown. The umbilicus is shallow and small, about 1/9-1/8 of the shell diameter; the umbilical margin is subangular, the umbilical wall low and steep. The septa are very closely spaced, the outer whorl having 21 septa; often the lobe of one suture meets the saddle of the next suture. In the suture, the ventral lobe is wide and short, divided into two ventral branches by a median saddle of medium height; the ventral branches lie at the ventrolateral margin, slightly expanded at the middle, pointed at the tip; the first lateral saddle is of medium height, its top slightly constricted and inclined slightly towards the venter; the first lateral lobe is twice as long as the ventral lobe, with 6-7 denticles of varying thickness at the tip; the second lateral saddle is higher than the first lateral saddle, its top wide and rounded; the second lateral lobe is fairly short and narrow, with five serrations at the lower part; the auxiliary lobe system comprises two small lobes, one of which is bifid at the tip.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Ziyun Miao and Bouyei Autonomous County, Guizhou, China
species.diagnosis: A fairly complete ammonite fossil, slightly damaged on the apertural side; the specimen is 6 cm long, 6 cm wide and 1 cm thick at maximum; the shell is small, semi-evolute, discoidal. The whorls overlap deeply, the cross-section long-elliptical. The venter is narrow and rounded, the flanks showing some flattening; the umbilicus is of medium width and depth. The surfaces of the venter and the ventrolateral parts are ornamented with even, fine longitudinal spiral striae and indistinct fold-like striae; the suture is not visible to the naked eye. Flemingites is classified in Animalia, Invertebrata, Mollusca, Cephalopoda, Ammonoidea; the suture of this group is very distinctive, consisting of a short, wide ventral lobe and two short, wide lateral lobes, the ventral lobe being divided by a very wide median saddle into two short, simple ventral branches. The lower end of the first lateral lobe has 8-10 prominent denticles arranged in an arc. The second lateral lobe is very short, lying outside the umbilical keel, with only a few denticles at the lower end. The auxiliary lobe system is very short, confined to the umbilical wall.

species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Small shell, involute and flattened discoidal, with the outer whorl growing rather rapidly. The whorl cross-section is a triangle with a rounded apex, width and height nearly equal. The venter is narrow and rounded; the flanks are broad and slightly arched, sloping toward the venter, with the greatest thickness at the umbilical margin. The shell surface is not preserved. The umbilicus is nearly closed. The ventral lobe of the suture is wide and divided into four branches; the inner branches are wider than the outer branches, with shallowly bifid ends, and the outer branches end in pointed wedge shapes. The lateral lobe is half as wide as the ventral lobe, bifid, and tongue-shaped with a pointed tip; its inner branch is wider and longer than its outer branch. The first and second lateral saddles are nearly equal in height, but the second lateral saddle is wide and rounded.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: vicinity of Zhaxizong Township, Tingri County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is robust and evolute, with a dome-shaped venter bearing a high, sharp median ventral keel, and a shallow longitudinal groove on either side of the keel; the whorl cross- section is slightly hexagonal. The umbilical wall is rather high and the umbilicus is rather large. The surface bears very distinct transverse ribs and two rows of tubercles. The transverse ribs form small tubercles at the umbilical margin, extend obliquely slightly backward from the umbilical margin, and form distinct tubercles at the ventrolateral margin. After the transverse ribs bifurcate regularly at the ventrolateral tubercles, they bend toward the front of the shell and disappear at the ventral longitudinal groove.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: the north mountain of Rongbo, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute, thick and thickly discoidal, with whorl overlap of about 1/3; the umbilicus is of medium size, with a steeply inclined umbilical wall; the flanks are flat, slightly convex in the middle, and converge rather rapidly toward the venter on the outer part; the venter is wide and flat, with a shallow ventral groove, and the whorl height is slightly greater than its thickness, the cross-section being squarish-rounded. The shell surface is ornamented with curved coarse ribs starting at the umbilical margin, with several patterns of distribution: in one kind, a rib starts from an umbilical tubercle and divides into two branches; in a second kind, a crest-like rib extends obliquely forward to the middle of the flanks and divides into two branches; in a third kind, a few single ribs are inserted; and in a fourth kind, a rib occasionally divides into two branches from an umbilical tubercle, one of which divides into two branches again in the middle of the flanks while the other does not branch further. The shell surface bears distinct umbilical tubercles, but their distribution is irregular. On the outer part of the whorl there are lateral tubercles; some ribs divide into two branches at the lateral tubercles, and some ribs bear both umbilical and lateral tubercles. The ribs on the inner whorls are finer, denser and more strongly curved, gradually becoming sparser and more robust and extending obliquely forward outward. All ribs terminate on either side of the venter, swelling into tubercles, and the whorl bears distinct constrictions.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: the north mountain of Rongbo, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell evolute, discoidal; whorls embrace about 1/3 of the preceding whorl. Umbilicus wide, umbilical wall steeply inclined; flanks slightly convex, venter flat with a shallow ventral groove. Whorl height slightly greater than thickness; whorl cross-section subquadrate-rounded. Shell surface ornamented with stout, ridge-like ribs. Ribs arise from the umbilical margin as single, ridge-like ribs slanting forward; they begin to bend backward at the middle of the flanks; a few ribs bifurcate at the umbilical margin. A few single intercalated ribs also occur; all ribs slant forward and terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, slightly swollen and nodose. A few indistinct constrictions occur on the flanks. The suture has a broad median ventral saddle and two narrow, small ventral lateral lobes, a broad first lateral lobe with a lateral branch and a long posterior branch, a short, small second lateral lobe, and a broad, high outer saddle subdivided by small lobules, among which a large lobe divides the saddle into two nearly equal parts; the first lateral saddle is narrow and low.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell evolute, thinly discoidal. The anteriormost part of the outer whorl has a rectangular cross-section. Flanks strongly compressed. Venter with a median ventral keel. The posterior part of the outer whorl has a narrowly arched venter, becoming toward the front a low, gently roof-shaped, nearly flat-topped form, and the ventrolateral margins correspondingly change from rounded to angular. The flanks are nearly flat, sloping gently toward the umbilicus near the umbilical margin. Umbilical margin rounded; umbilicus wide, about 1/3 of the shell diameter. The flanks of the inner whorls are smooth or bear weak transverse ribbing. From the posterior part of the outer whorl to the posterior part of the body chamber, the transverse ribs on the flanks gradually become coarser, then rapidly become weaker and denser, bending slightly forward at the inner- middle part of the flanks and slightly backward near the ventrolateral margin, their starting points gradually moving away from the umbilical margin. The transverse ribs generally become coarser outward. The external suture: ventral lobe fairly long, bifid, ventral lateral lobe narrow and pointed; lateral lobe narrow and long, its lower end bearing 8-9 denticles of varying size; first umbilical lobe rather short, its lower end bearing 6-7 denticles. External saddle low and broad; lateral saddle highest.

species.diagnosis: Shell medium-large, semi-evolute, flatly discoidal. Whorl cross-section semi-elliptical, flanks compressed. The holotype has a shell diameter of 34 mm, whorl height 14 mm and thickness about 10 mm. Venter arched and rounded, smooth. Ventrolateral part rounded, flanks slightly convex. Umbilicus wide, about 2/5 of the shell diameter, umbilical margin fairly rounded, umbilical wall low and steep. Flanks with fine ribs slanting forward, arising from the umbilical margin, gradually thickening outward, reaching their coarsest at the middle of the flanks, then gradually weakening outward again, bending forward and rapidly disappearing. The external suture: ventral lobe slightly constricted in the upper part, ventral lateral lobe slightly expanded in the middle, constricted in the lower part, with 2-3 fine denticles at the lower end; lateral lobe very long, palmate, markedly constricted in the upper part and markedly expanded in the lower part, with 9-10 fine denticles at the lower end; first umbilical lobe narrow and short, slightly constricted in the upper part, with 6-7 fine denticles at the lower end. External saddle slightly lower than the lateral saddle, both onion-shaped, constricted to varying degrees in the lower part, the former especially so.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small and thickly discoidal, evolute in the juvenile stage and semi-evolute in the adult stage. The whorl cross-section is crescent-shaped; the height is 1/5 of the width. The venter is broad and rounded; the flanks are rather narrow. The umbilicus is fairly large, 1/2 of the shell diameter. The flanks bear growth lines and longitudinal spiral lines. The growth lines are fine and dense, arising from the umbilical margin, convex forward at the ventrolateral margin, and forming a shallow ventral sinus as they cross the venter. The longitudinal lines are less developed than the growth lines. The outer whorl has two shallow constrictions. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is narrow, divided into two branches by a low median ventral saddle; the lateral lobe is broadly V-shaped, with a smoothly rounded end; the umbilical lobe is on the umbilical wall, funnel-shaped.

species.distribution: Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and discoidal, with compressed flanks. The whorl cross-section is elliptical; the venter is narrow and rounded; the flanks are slightly convex. The umbilical margin is prominent and angular; the umbilical wall is steep and vertical. The outer whorl embraces the inner whorl to about 1/2 of its height, and is impressed into it by 1/3 of the whorl height. The height of the outermost whorl is about 2/5 of the shell diameter, and its thickness is slightly more than half of the height. The width of the umbilicus is about 2/7 of the diameter. The surface bears curved folds parallel to the growth lines; these wrinkles arise from the umbilical seam, curve backward on the flanks, turn forward near the venter, and cross the venter without interruption. On the inner part of the outermost whorl of the holotype there are also tubercles; these tubercles are most prominent at the umbilical margin, elongating and widening toward the middle of the flanks. The suture is of the ceratitic type, with complete saddles and dentate lobes. The ventral lobe is broad and short, divided by a ventral saddle into two ventral branches, each bearing a few teeth at the lower end. The first lateral lobe is the longest, about twice the ventral lobe; the second lateral lobe is slightly longer than the ventral lobe, but narrower. The rib line bears a few teeth and becomes a broad, shallow lobe on the umbilical wall.

F001000346; collected at Xindianzi, Shahe Town, Chaotian District, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China. species.diagnosis: The shell is small, involute and flatly discoidal. The venter is narrow and rounded; the flanks slope toward the venter; the maximum thickness is at the umbilical margin. The shell surface bears fine growth lines. The umbilicus is nearly closed. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is broad, composed of two pairs of adventitious lobes, each pair bearing two teeth; the second pair of adventitious lobes is slightly longer than the first pair; the sides of the median ventral saddle are nearly parallel, its height exceeding half the length of the ventral lobe; the adventitious saddle is half as high as the median ventral saddle, with a smoothly rounded top; the lateral lobe is broad and bifid, the inner branch longer than the outer branch, each ending in two small teeth; the first lateral saddle is high with a rounded top; the second lateral saddle is broad and rounded. The septa are closely spaced, with 4 sutures within 5 mm.

species.diagnosis: This species is very similar to the species of Tongluceras, but its suture is simpler: there are only 4 pairs of external lateral lobes, and the teeth on the ventral branches and lateral lobes are less developed than in the latter — not only are there fewer teeth, but the teeth are generally developed only at the posterior part or posterior end of the lobes. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell diameter may exceed 90 mm, evolute, thickly discoidal. The venter of the inner whorls is unknown; on the posterior part of the outer whorl the venter appears broadly arched, becoming flatter toward the anterior part, with a prominent median ventral keel. The flanks of the inner whorls slope toward the umbilicus, becoming flat toward the middle-anterior part of the outer whorl. Umbilicus broad. The flanks of the inner whorls bear weak transverse ribs and ventrolateral nodes. From the penultimate whorl onward, coarse short transverse ribs appear, arising at the umbilical margin, thickening and rising sharply outward, and ending at the ventrolateral margin in very coarse, highly raised longitudinal nodes. As the whorl grows, ribs and nodes become more massive; toward the middle-anterior part of the outer whorl, as the flanks flatten, the transverse ribs and nodes weaken. The ribs originate farther from the umbilical margin, retreating outward. The largest ventrolateral longitudinal node is 7-8 mm high and 10 mm long.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell of medium size, shell diameter about 52 mm, evolute, thinly discoidal. Whorl cross- section slightly rectangular, whorl height 22 mm, whorl thickness 13 mm, flanks strongly compressed. Venter narrow and smooth, arched and rounded, with a prominent median ventral keel. Flanks flat, umbilicus rather shallow, umbilical width 1/3 of the shell diameter, umbilical margin rather rounded, umbilical wall low. The flanks of the anterior part of the penultimate whorl bear fine dense ribs; with growth the ribs gradually become coarser, arising at the umbilical margin, thickening slightly outward, and ending at the ventrolateral margin. From the middle part of the outer whorl onward, the transverse ribs end at the ventrolateral margin in small nodes. On the anterior part of the outer whorl the transverse ribs are finer and curve slightly forward. The external suture: the ventral lobe is broad above and narrows downward, divided by the ventral saddle into two narrow pointed ventral branches, with two teeth at the lower end; the lateral lobe is rather long, its sides nearly parallel, with 7-8 teeth at the lower end; the first umbilical lobe is short, narrowing slightly downward, with 5-6 teeth at the lower end. The external saddle is the highest, narrow above and broad below; the lateral saddle is lower than the external saddle; the umbilical saddle is low and broadly rounded.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Lajiashan, Jiajia County, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell of medium to large size, involute, rather thickly discoidal, with even growth during ontogeny; venter broadly rounded, ventral margin bluntly rounded, flanks slightly convex and nearly flat, greatest width near the ventral margin; in the late adult stage the whorls may have a flat venter. Umbilicus small and deep, umbilical margin narrowly rounded, umbilical wall narrow and convex. No longitudinal ornament, with beautiful comb-like growth lines, starting at the umbilical margin, fine and dense at first, becoming sparser and coarser toward the venter, partly bifurcating, curving in an 'S' shape on the flanks, and when crossing the venter strongly convex posteriorly, bending on the venter in a triangular shape. Goniatitic suture; the ventral lobe is very broad; the ventral branches are also very broad and deep. About twice as wide as the first lateral lobe or one and a half times the median ventral saddle, divided into five tooth-like parts, the middle tooth strong and finger-like, the marginal teeth often underdeveloped, only slightly curved; the median ventral saddle is high like a pillar, about 2/3 as high as the external saddle; all lobes are divided only to the middle of the saddle, the middle part strongly constricted, the upper part complete, subglobose or mushroom-shaped; the external saddle is the highest, the other saddles decreasing in height in sequence toward the umbilicus, like a slope; among the external lobes, except for the 2-3 near the umbilical margin that are pointed, the other lobes show finger-like division to varying degrees, the strongest division being in the first three outer lateral lobes. There are 7-8 lobes between the external saddle and the umbilicus.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Dagangping Village, Yangchun City, Yangjiang City, Guangdong Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell large, involute, subglobose or thickly discoidal, the outer whorl completely embracing the inner whorl, the inner whorl embedded to about 1/2 the height of the outer whorl; venter narrowly arched, ventrolateral margin broadly rounded, flanks broad and gently convex, greatest shell width at the umbilical margin, width slightly greater than height, whorl cross-section nearly saddle-shaped or horseshoe-shaped. Umbilicus small and deep, umbilical margin rounded, umbilical wall steep and slightly inclined, gently convex. Body chamber nearly one whorl long, the outer whorl bearing 5 broad shallow band-like constrictions. Ornament weak, shell surface nearly smooth. The suture: the ventral lobe is broad and trough-like, slightly swollen at the lower end, divided by a short columnar median ventral saddle into two shovel-shaped ventral branches; the median ventral saddle is about as wide as the ventral branches, about 1/3 of the ventral lobe, and about 2/5 as high as the external saddle; two tooth-like outer lateral lobes, the first outer lateral lobe the widest, the second outer lateral lobe the longest, and the branches of the third outer lateral lobe having become nearly independent two-toothed lobes; the umbilical lobe is broad, with 3 small teeth at the base of the lobe. The saddles are complete, with rounded tops, columnar, the saddles decreasing slightly in height and width from outside inward, arranged nearly in a straight line.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell of medium size, discoidal, nearly involute. Venter narrowly rounded. Whorl cross- section semi-elliptical, height 4/5 of the width or the two nearly equal. Flanks slightly arched. Umbilicus small, umbilical diameter about 1/4 of the shell diameter, umbilical margin angular, umbilical wall low and steep. Shell surface ornamented with fine transverse striae, arising at the umbilical margin, weakly 'S'-shaped, bending backward at the venter to form a broad shallow ventral sinus. Each whorl bears 3 constrictions; in a few specimens the constrictions are absent. The external suture: the ventral lobe is rather broad, divided by a moderately high bottle-shaped median ventral saddle into two branches, the ventral branches spear-shaped; the lateral lobe is shorter than the ventral lobe at an early stage, inverted-helmet-shaped, and slightly longer than the ventral lobe in the adult stage, slightly swollen in the middle; the first lateral saddle is high, with an arched rounded top; the second lateral saddle is slightly lower than the first, broadly rounded and asymmetrical; the umbilical lobe is located on the umbilical wall, shallowly funnel-shaped.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Small shell, nearly involute, thickly discoidal. The venter is narrow and dome-shaped. The whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical, the flanks compressed, height approximately equal to width. The flanks incline slightly toward the venter. The umbilicus is small, about 1/5 of the shell diameter; the umbilical margin is subangular. Reticulate ornament; the umbilical margin bears small nodes. The transverse striae are fine and dense, 22 within 5 mm. The transverse striae start from the umbilical nodes, bend backward toward the middle of the flank, then bend strongly forward at the ventrolateral region in a clear 'S' shape, and bend backward again when crossing the venter, forming a wide, deep ventral sinus; the longitudinal striae are well developed, those on the ventrolateral region slightly coarser than those on the flanks and venter. The outer whorl bears 3–4 constrictions. The external suture: the ventral lobe is moderately wide; the low, wide median saddle divides the ventral lobe into two prongs, the ventral prongs nearly parallel on the two sides, tongue- shaped; the lateral lobe is fairly wide, inverted helmet-shaped, with a fairly rounded end; the first lateral saddle is wider than the lateral lobe, with a rounded top; the second lateral saddle is wide and flat, asymmetrical.

The venter is broad and rounded, the flanks narrow and flatly rounded. The shell surface bears a reticulate ornament; the growth lines start from the umbilical wall, incline slightly forward as they cross the flanks, and form a shallow ventral sinus at the venter, while the longitudinal spiral striae are very well developed. Each whorl bears three shallow constrictions. The umbilicus is fairly large, about 1/2 of the shell diameter, with a low, steep umbilical wall and a rounded umbilical margin. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: west of Kadong Village, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and flatly discoidal, the whorls embracing about 1/3, the umbilicus broad and narrow, with a steep umbilical wall. The shell surface bears fine, dense, radially arranged transverse ribs; the ribs start from the umbilical wall, most of them being single ribs that bifurcate in the middle of the flanks, with a few ribs not bifurcating. On the outer whorl, the ribs incline forward and curve slightly, and the branching points swell to form ridged nodes. All the ribs end at the sides of the ventral groove. The suture has a broad ventral saddle, its top divided into two parts by a small lobe, the two sides splitting in a serrated manner. The ventral branches are slender and long, the first lateral lobe is large, with symmetrical lateral branches and a slender terminal branch, the second lateral lobe is short and small, and two umbilical lobes are visible on the umbilical wall. The external saddle is broad, divided into equal parts by a secondary lobe; the first lateral saddle is narrower than the external saddle, divided by a secondary lobe into two unequal parts, the inner higher and the outer lower; the second lateral saddle is relatively low and small, its top bearing 3-4 lobules.

species.distribution: the north mountain of Rongbo, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell diameter 46 mm, semi-evolute, the shell fairly thick and discoidal, the whorls embracing nearly 1/2, the umbilicus fairly small, 14 mm, with a steep umbilical wall. The two sides are flat, slightly convex in the middle, and the outer part contracts broadly toward the venter. The venter is flat and rounded, with a shallow ventral groove. The whorl width and thickness are almost equal, the maximum thickness being at the umbilical nodes, and the cross-section is subquadrate. The shell surface bears fine, dense, radially arranged transverse ribs with nodes, regularly distributed; the ribs start from the umbilical wall, bifurcating at the umbilical nodes, one of the ribs bifurcating again at the lateral nodes; all the ribs end at the sides of the venter, slightly swollen but not forming nodes. The umbilical nodes are elongate and rhombic, arranged correspondingly with the lateral nodes.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Changjianggou, Shangsi Township, Jiange County, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: Well preserved, shell of medium size, shell diameter about 55 mm, evolute and discoidal, the body chamber half a whorl long. The venter is roof-shaped, the two sides flattened and constricted; in the juvenile stage the sides incline inward, the last two whorls gradually becoming flat, and in the adult stage slightly convex, the part near the umbilical margin raised and inclined slightly outward. The maximum thickness is near the umbilical margin; the umbilicus is fairly shallow, the umbilical width about 2/5 of the shell diameter, the umbilical margin indistinct, and the umbilical wall inclined inward. In the juvenile stage the shell bears sparse, stout transverse ribs, the ribs starting from the umbilical suture and becoming coarser outward, forming stout rounded nodes at the ventrolateral margin; as the whorls grow, the transverse ribs become finer and the ventrolateral nodes correspondingly smaller; in the second half of the outer whorl the transverse ribs become finer and denser and the ventrolateral nodes even smaller; toward the front part of the outer whorl the transverse ribs become slightly coarser, inclining slightly forward at the ventrolateral part, the rib spacing increasing and the ventrolateral nodes becoming larger, and near the aperture the ribs and nodes gradually disappear. The external suture has a moderately large ventral lobe, bipartite, the ventral branches without denticles; the lateral lobe is long, slightly constricted in the upper part, with 5-6 denticles at the lower end; the umbilical lobe is short, about 1/2 as long as the lateral lobe, with 5-6 denticles at the lower end; the top of the first lateral saddle is constricted and rounded-pointed; the second lateral saddle is slightly higher than the first lateral saddle, with a rounded top; the umbilical saddle is higher than the two saddles above, asymmetrical, inclined toward the umbilicus.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: east bank of Chaiqu, Zhongba County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Only one incomplete specimen is known; the shell is fairly large (d approx. 56 mm), involute and subglobose, the outer whorl almost completely embracing the inner whorl, the venter arched and rounded, the ventrolateral part broad and rounded, the two sides gently convex, with no clear boundary between them, the maximum shell width in the middle of the flanks. The umbilicus is closed, with a fairly distinct low depression around the umbilical centre. The ornament is weak and the shell surface is nearly smooth. The simple goniatitic suture has a fairly shallow, nearly V-shaped ventral lobe; the external saddle is broad, with a broad, shallow adventitious lobe, the adventitious lobe being shorter than the ventral and lateral lobes. The lateral lobe is fairly broad and slightly asymmetrical, shaped like an inverted bell; the lateral saddle is slightly lower than the external saddle, asymmetrical and broadly arched.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Geological Museum of China, specimen no. IV11548, resource no. species.diagnosis: Two specimens preserved as whorl fragments, from which the shell can be inferred to be thinly discoidal and nearly involute. The shell is not preserved and no ornament is seen. The umbilicus is fairly small, the umbilical wall low and slightly inclined, the umbilical margin rounded. The ventral lobe of the external suture is slightly expanded in the middle, its end divided into three narrow, pointed branches, the middle branch slightly longer than the two sides; the lateral lobe is broader than the ventral lobe, its lower part divided into two nearly symmetrical branches; the umbilical lobe is narrow, long and pointed, slightly expanded in the middle-lower part, becoming successively shorter toward the umbilicus; the first lateral saddle is low and narrow, the second lateral saddle slightly higher than the other saddles, with a smoothly rounded saddle top.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Tulong, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is involute and nearly globose, dorsoventrally compressed. The venter is broad and rounded, the flanks arched and rounded, grading into the venter. The whorl cross- section is semicircular, the umbilicus closed. The shell surface is densely covered with nearly radial transverse ribs, the ribs single or bifurcating, curving slightly forward on the venter to form a broad ventral ridge. The suture is of the ammonitic type, the denticles complex and finger-like, invading the saddles to a great height. The external lobe is narrow and long, divided by a narrow median saddle into two branches; the lateral lobe is fairly deep, and the umbilical lobe is not very clear.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Yanhu Town, Changning City, Hengyang City, Hunan Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small, evolute and thinly discoidal, with a broad, shallow umbilicus. The venter is arched and rounded, the two flanks parallel, the umbilical wall arcuate, the dorsum slightly compressed, and the whorl cross-section elongate and subrectangular. In the early growth stages the shell surface bears nodose rib ornament; on the outer whorl, the shell surface is dominated by rather dense transverse ribbing, mainly confined to the flanks, slightly projecting forward at the ventrolateral and umbilical margins. In the suture, the ventral lobe is rather deeply bifid; the first lateral lobe (l) is deep and rounded; the second lateral lobe (i) lies near the umbilicus, with a rounded base, about half as deep as the first lateral lobe; the umbilical small lobe (i') is developed. In some specimens, a few incipient small denticles are faintly visible at the base of the lateral lobe.

species.distribution: Jintanbu, Lengwu, Tonglu County, Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province, China
species.diagnosis: This species is close to Mexicoceras, since the latter also has five pairs of lateral lobes, and differs considerably from Waagenoceras, which has 6-8 pairs of lateral lobes. But its lobes branch far more simply: on the inner side of the ventral branch lobe there are only two short protuberance-like denticles, and none on the outer side; the first pair of lateral lobes has five digitate denticles, the second to fifth pairs have 4-5 denticles, which do not encroach upon the rounded saddles; the saddles are slightly arched, differing from Mexicoceras.

species.diagnosis: Judging by the number of lobes, the suture of this species should be assigned to Meicoceras, but the denticles of its lobes are far simpler than in the latter, indicating its primitive nature, and it is therefore placed in this genus. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small, involute and flattened discoidal; the outer whorl increases rapidly in height, its cross-section a tall triangle with a rounded top, the width being four-fifths of the height. The venter is narrow and dome-shaped. The flanks are broad and slightly arched, sloping from the dorsum toward the venter, the greatest thickness lying at the umbilical margin. The shell surface bears fine growth lines or is smooth. The umbilicus is almost closed. The ventral lobe of the external suture is broad and four-parted; the ventral branch lobes are slightly broad, slightly constricted in the middle, and both end in bifurcations, the outer branch being broader than the inner branch but shorter; the median ventral saddle is narrow, rather high and bottle-shaped; the lateral lobe is a deep pointed 'V' shape, its inner side curving in an arc; the first lateral saddle is high, its top slightly constricted; the second lateral saddle is broad and rounded, sloping toward the umbilicus. The septa are crowded, with five suture lines within 5 mm.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is nearly involute and discoidal. The venter is narrow and rounded. The whorl cross-section is horseshoe-shaped, height and width nearly equal. The flanks are slightly dome-shaped, sloping toward the venter, the greatest thickness lying at the umbilical margin. The umbilicus is rather small, one-fifth of the shell diameter, with angular umbilical margins and a steep umbilical wall. The shell surface is ornamented with fine transverse striae, with small tubercles at the umbilical margin. Each whorl bears three constrictions. In the suture, the ventral lobe is rather broad, divided into two branches by a moderately high median ventral saddle; the ventral branch lobes are tongue-shaped, their sides nearly parallel, the lower part of the outer side slightly expanded, the ends rather rounded; the lateral lobe is broad and 'V'-shaped; the first lateral saddle is about as wide as the lateral lobe, its top rounded and slightly constricted; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall and is shallow and funnel-shaped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. X0152-15, resource no. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is large, evolute and thinly discoidal. The umbilicus is large and shallow, with a short, steeply sloping umbilical wall and a rounded, indistinct umbilical margin. The outermost whorl grows rapidly, its degree of enclosure being between about one-half and one-third. The flanks are flat, the venter narrow and rounded. The greatest thickness of the whorl lies at the umbilical shoulder, its height being far greater than its width, the cross-section a tall, elongate-ovate shape. The surface is ornamented with strong, coarse ribs extending obliquely forward, forming bundles of 4-5 branch ribs; at the front of the body chamber, between each long rib there are 8-9 short ribs; all ribs become thicker on the venter and cross it. The ribs of the inner whorls are fine and dense, all bifurcating.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is rather small, 7.8-14 mm in shell diameter, semi-evolute and discoidal. The whorl cross-section is nearly semicircular, the height being seven-tenths of the width. The venter bears a shallow, flat ventral groove in the middle, which gradually disappears in the adult stage, becoming dome-shaped and rounded. The ventrolateral margins are smoothly rounded, with a weak ventrolateral groove appearing in the adult stage. The flanks slope slightly toward the venter. The umbilicus is of medium size, about one-third of the shell diameter, with rounded umbilical margins and a low, steep umbilical wall. The shell surface is ornamented with fine transverse ribs inclined forward, forming a ventrolateral projection at the ventrolateral margin, without crossing the venter. The transverse ribs arise at the umbilical margin and swell into small tubercles there. Some transverse ribs merge, two or three into one, toward the inner middle part of the flanks. The outer whorl bears four shallow constrictions. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is rather broad, with narrow, short ventral branch lobes; the first lateral lobe is a narrow 'V' shape; the first lateral saddle is broad and high, with a rounded saddle top; the second lateral saddle is low; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall and is shallow and funnel-shaped.

F001000297; collected at Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China. species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small, nearly evolute and discoidal. The whorl cross-section is a transversely semi-elliptical shape, the whorl height being one-half of the width. The venter is rather broad, with a shallow, flat ventral groove in the middle and rounded ventrolateral margins. The flanks are rather narrow and slightly arched, sloping toward the venter. The umbilicus is rather large, about one-half of the shell diameter. The shell surface is ornamented with low, fine transverse ribs inclined forward, which bend backward at the ventrolateral margin and terminate there. The transverse ribs swell into small tubercles at the umbilical margin. The outer whorl bears 3-4 shallow constrictions. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is rather broad, shallowly three-parted at the end, the middle denticle being slightly longer than those on either side; the first lateral lobe is 'V'-shaped, its height only one-half that of the ventral lobe; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall and is shallow and funnel-shaped.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: France
species.diagnosis: The shell is rather small, 48 mm in diameter. The umbilicus is of medium size, about one- third of the shell diameter, with a gently sloping umbilical wall and an indistinct umbilical margin. The flanks are slightly convex, the venter broad and rounded, the whorl height greater than the thickness, the greatest thickness lying at the umbilical shoulder. The shell surface is ornamented with single and branching transverse ribs; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin, some bifurcating at the umbilical margin with the branching point slightly swollen but not forming a tubercle. All ribs gradually become thicker outward from the umbilical margin, being thickest at the ventrolateral margins and on the venter, and all cross the venter.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Geoscience Museum of Kunming University of Science and Technology, specimen no. ZJ-FR-0002, resource no. F001003586; collected at France. species.diagnosis: The shell is thickly ellipsoid, nearly involute, with a rounded venter; the greatest thickness is about two-thirds of the shell diameter; the whorl cross-section is helmet-shaped, and the surface is ornamented with longitudinal spiral striae and growth lines. The external suture consists of five lobes and the same number of saddles. The ventral lobe is divided by a bottle-shaped median ventral saddle into two long, spear-shaped branch lobes; the lateral lobes are three-forked, forming three narrow, pointed 'V'-shaped lobes, the two side branch lobes being shorter than the middle one. The external saddle resembles the branches of the ventral lobe, slightly broader, sloping toward the lateral lobes. The first lateral saddle forms a broad arc. The umbilical lobe is undeveloped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. YF0714, resource no. F001005470; collected at Dewu, Shuicheng County, Liupanshui City, Guizhou Province, China. Age, locality and description follow the NIMRF record of the illustrated specimen; order and family are not verified from that source.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell form and ornament change markedly during ontogeny. Small to medium specimens (less than 30 mm in shell diameter) are flattened discoidal and semi-involute. The whorl cross-section is transversely kidney-shaped. The venter is dome-shaped and rounded, the flanks rather narrow, sloping toward the venter. The umbilicus is of medium size; the transverse ribs at the umbilical margin are fine and short. The growth lines are clear, the longitudinal lines weak. Each whorl bears three constrictions. Large shells (30-80 mm) are flattened discoidal and semi-involute. The whorl cross-section is rounded- triangular. The venter is narrow and rounded. The flanks are rather broad. The greatest thickness lies at the umbilical margin. The umbilicus is rather small, slightly less than one- quarter of the shell diameter in width, with an angular umbilical margin and a rather high, steep umbilical wall. The umbilical ribs gradually disappear as the shell grows; the shell surface is ornamented with wavy, fine, dense longitudinal and transverse striae, the transverse striae forming a broad, deep ventral sinus at the venter. The constrictions have disappeared on adult shells. In the external suture, the ventral lobe is broad, with a rather broad median ventral saddle half as high as the ventral lobe; in juvenile individuals the lateral lobe is inverted-helmet-shaped, its outer side slightly expanded, becoming a narrow 'V' shape in the adult stage; the first lateral saddle is broad with a rather rounded top; the second lateral saddle is broad, rounded and asymmetrical; the umbilical lobe lies at the umbilical margin and is funnel-shaped.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Xiaoyuchuan, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small, thickly discoidal and evolute. The venter is rounded, with slight compression between venter and dorsum. The umbilical margin is the thickest part of the shell, and the umbilicus is broad. There is a longitudinal groove on the ventrolateral part; the shell surface is ornamented with fine striae, which bend backward at the venter to form a ventral sinus, and project forward at the longitudinal groove on the ventrolateral part. The umbilical margin bears many short transverse ribs curving forward, which form tubercular protuberances that disappear near the longitudinal groove. The suture is unknown.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, evolute and discoidal. The cross-section of the outer whorl is nearly rectangular. The venter is narrow, dome-shaped and rounded, with a median ventral keel. The flanks of the inner whorls are steeply sloping. The shell bears robust transverse ribs and coarse ventrolateral tubercles. Toward the middle of the outer whorl, the transverse ribs on the flanks suddenly become finer and longer, and the ventrolateral tubercles weaken. The suture is of ammonitic type, with a bipartite ventral lobe, the ventral branch lobes slightly bifurcated, with two lateral lobes and a very short umbilical lobe series.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. YF0619, resource no. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is flattened globose and involute; the whorl cross-section is horseshoe-shaped. The venter is broad and rounded, the flanks flat and rounded. The umbilicus is very small, with a low and steeply inclined umbilical wall. The shell surface bears longitudinal lines, growth lines and constrictions. The longitudinal lines are dense and uniform. The growth lines are fine, dense and rather straight. The constrictions are narrow and deep, becoming wider towards the mid-flank. In the external suture the ventral lobe is rather wide; the lateral lobe is inverted-bell-shaped; the top of the first lateral saddle is constricted and rounded; the second lateral saddle is wide and higher than the first lateral saddle.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. YF0408, resource no. F001005168; collected at Chenmazijing, Zhongning County, Zhongwei City, Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, China. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Tuyukerishi, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is medium-sized, thickly cake-shaped to flattened globose, and involute. The outer whorl encloses one-half of the height of the inner whorl. The whorl width exceeds the whorl height, and the whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical. The umbilicus is rather small and moderately deep; the umbilical margin is rather rounded, the umbilical wall moderately high and rather steep. The test shows rather well-developed curved transverse striae, which form a shallow ventral sinus on the venter, together with weak longitudinal striae. In the external suture the ventral lobe is moderately wide, widening distinctly upwards; the median saddle is moderately high (less than one-half of the ventral lobe); the ventral lateral lobe is knife-shaped; the lateral lobe is wider than the ventral lobe and helmet-shaped; the umbilical lobe is narrow and short, situated on the umbilical wall; the external saddle is narrow and pointed, inclined slightly towards the umbilicus; the lateral saddle is rather wide and low, asymmetrical on the two sides.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is large, evolute and discoidal. The outermost whorl grows rather rapidly, with an involution of less than 1/3. The umbilical wall is rather steep, the umbilical margin distinct, the venter broad and flat, with a distinct concave median ventral groove, the groove being rather shallow and narrow; the flanks are flat, slightly convex at the mid- flanks, and the greatest whorl thickness is at the umbilical shoulder, the cross-section being a tall ellipse. The surface is ornamented with radiate, straight ribs extending obliquely forwards, with wide intercostal grooves; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate outwards at the mid-flanks to one-third of the way to the outer margin, with occasional single ribs inserted. In some specimens the transverse ribs bend forwards between one-half of the flanks and one-third of the way to the outer margin; all ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove and swell, but without forming small tubercles.

species.diagnosis: The shell is small, evolute and discoidal, with an involution of about 1/4 to slightly less than 1/3. The umbilicus is concave and open, the umbilical wall steep, the venter rather flat, with a distinct ventral groove extending to the end of the shell. The flanks are rather flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, and the whorl cross-section is a tall rectangle. The shell surface is ornamented with sharp-crested radiate ribs, which arise at the umbilical margin and extend obliquely outwards, bending at the outer margin and bifurcating, the bifurcation point being about between the mid-flanks and one-third of the way to the outer margin. The ribs are widely spaced, with many single ribs irregularly inserted among them. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, swelling to form tall, small spine-like tubercles.

species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is medium-sized and thin, thinly discoidal. The umbilicus is medium-sized, slightly more than one-third of the shell diameter, the umbilical wall inclined, the umbilical margin rounded but indistinct. The whorls grow at a moderate rate, with an involution of about one-third to one-quarter. The venter is broad, with a wide median ventral groove extending to the body chamber, but becoming indistinct near the aperture. The flanks are flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, and the whorl cross-section is rectangular. The shell surface is ornamented with forward-curving transverse ribs, denser on the inner whorls and sparser on the outer whorls, especially so in the body chamber. The ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate at the mid-flanks; on the outermost part of the outer whorl the bifurcation point is close to the inner side, and the ribs are more strongly curved. The ribs thicken and project at the bifurcation. Single ribs are occasionally inserted on the whorls; the intercostal grooves are uniform, but constrictions appear near the aperture and the intercostal grooves deepen. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, projecting as spines, especially so in the body chamber.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and discoidal. The whorls grow moderately, with an involution of one- third. The umbilicus is medium-sized, about one-third of the shell diameter, shallow, with a rather steeply inclined umbilical wall and an indistinct, fully rounded umbilical margin. The flanks are rather flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, and the whorl cross-section is ovate. The venter is rather broad, with a wide and shallow median ventral groove. The shell surface is ornamented with radiate, straight transverse ribs inclined slightly forwards. The suture: too strongly eroded and poorly preserved, but its main characters are still clear. The ventral saddle is low and narrow, the ventral lateral lobe small, the external saddle wide, divided in the middle by a small leaflet into two identical parts; the first lateral lobe is thick and large, with a three-branched tail, and long. The first lateral saddle is narrower than the external saddle, likewise cut by a small leaflet. The second lateral lobe is narrow and short, slanting outwards. The auxiliary series is fine, already divided into saddles and lobes.

species.distribution: about 2 km southeast of Langnongla Pass, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and thickly discoidal, with a broad, arched venter. The whorl cross- section is subquadrate. The transverse ribs are slightly curved, bifurcating at about one- third of the whorl height near the umbilical margin, occasionally trifurcating. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Lajiashan, Jiajia County, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is rather small, involute and subglobose. The venter is arched and rounded, the ventrolateral margin broad and rounded, merging with the venter; the flanks are gently convex, the greatest width being at the mid-flanks. The umbilicus is small and deep, the umbilical margin broad and rounded, joining the umbilical wall in a slope down to the umbilical seam. The shell surface is ornamented with fine, dense longitudinal spiral lines; at a whorl height of 8 mm there are 11-12 lines per 3 mm; the constrictions are weak, starting at the umbilical seam, bending slightly backwards at the mid-flanks and venter and slightly forwards at the ventrolateral margin, with 3-4(?) on the outer whorl. In the suture the ventral lobe is wide, the ventral lateral lobes wide, rounded and fan-shaped; the median saddle is tall but slightly lower than the external saddle, its width nearly equal to the widths of the ventral lateral lobe and the external saddle; the septal neck is long, about 1/3 of the chamber; there are three outer lateral lobes, the first two wide and rounded, slightly wider than the saddles, the third outer lateral lobe shallower, narrow- tongue-shaped; the external saddle and the outer lateral saddle are both rounded, with little difference in height. The second lateral saddle is narrow and compressed-tongue- shaped, short and inclined slightly towards the venter; the third lateral saddle is wide, asymmetrically arched and rounded; the umbilical lobe is wide and shallow.
