species.distribution: below Douyu Bridge, Aoquan Town, Guiyang County, Chenzhou City, Hunan Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is semi-evolute and thickly discoidal, with a rather wide umbilicus, u/d = 0.39. The venter is broad and rounded, the boundary between the venter and the flanks indistinct, the outer margin of the whorl cross-section elliptical, the dorsum slightly compressed. The umbilicus is rather deep, with a nearly vertical umbilical wall. Deep, wide intercostal grooves near the umbilical margin cut into the shell surface, forming robust radiate short ribs, about 21 ribs on the outer whorl. The shell surface is covered all over with longitudinal spiral striae, about 41 in total on the venter and flanks, absent on the umbilical wall. The outer whorl has five constrictions, which together with weak growth lines form a wide, shallow ventral sinus on the venter. In the suture the two sides of the ventral lobe are nearly parallel, the lateral lobe is inverted-bell-shaped, the umbilical lobe rather pointed and deep; the median saddle is very wide, swollen at the top, and the top of the external saddle is also rather wide.

The whorl cross-section is circular. The shell surface is ornamented with fine, dense transverse ribs; on the inner whorls the ribs are very regularly distributed, while in the body chamber a few constrictions begin to appear, making the rib distribution less regular, in particular making the intercostal grooves vary in width and bending the transverse ribs forwards. All ribs arise at the umbilical margin, bifurcate outwards at one-third of the way to the outer side, and incline forwards; occasionally a rib bifurcates at the umbilical margin, and very few single ribs are inserted; all ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, slightly swollen, but without forming small tubercles. The suture: poorly preserved. The ventral saddle is wide, the ventral lateral lobe short, the external saddle wide, divided by a small leaflet into two equal parts; the first lateral lobe is wide, large and long, three-branched at the end, with a pointed, long tail. The first lateral saddle is narrower than the external saddle, divided by a small leaflet into two parts; the second lateral lobe is short and small, slanting outwards. The auxiliary series is simple, the saddles and lobes distinct, but only slightly divided.

species.diagnosis: The shell is rather large, evolute and thickly discoidal, the outer whorl growing rather rapidly, with an involution of one-third. The flanks are flat, the greatest whorl thickness is at the umbilical shoulder, the whorl height being distinctly greater than the thickness, the cross-section rectangular. The venter is broad and flat, with a wide and shallow ventral groove. The shell surface is ornamented with radiate, strong, dense transverse ribs curving slightly forwards; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate outwards slightly beyond the mid-flanks, the bifurcation point slightly thickened, more distinctly so in some ribs and less so in others. No single ribs are inserted in the preserved whorls. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, swelling to form small tubercle-like projections, with occasional irregular large tubercles formed by the junction of two ribs. The suture: with a wide and tall ventral saddle, a narrow and slender ventral lateral lobe, and a wide, large external saddle, divided by a slender, much-branched small leaflet into two symmetrical parts; the second lateral lobe is short and small, slanting inwards. The auxiliary series is fine and indistinct. The suture characters are the same as those of the type of the genus Berriasella.

species.diagnosis: The shell is small, thin and flat, thinly discoidal. The whorls grow uniformly, with an involution of 1/4. The umbilicus is large, slightly more than one-third of the shell diameter, the umbilical wall gently inclined, the umbilical margin fully rounded but indistinct. The venter is rounded, with a distinct shallow median ventral groove. The flanks are flat, slightly convex at the mid-flanks, and the whorl cross-section is circular, but the height slightly exceeds the thickness. The shell surface is ornamented with fine, dense transverse ribs extending obliquely forwards and curving slightly; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate outwards at one-third of the way to the outer margin, curving forwards. On the inner whorls the bifurcating ribs and the inserted single ribs occur in a clustered pattern and are regularly distributed. On the outer whorl the ribs vary more; a few ribs bifurcate at the umbilical margin and then again at one-third of the way to the outer margin, one of them bifurcating a second time, the inserted single ribs being irregularly distributed, with constrictions appearing from time to time. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, slightly thickened, but without forming nodes or tubercles.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: the north mountain of Rongbo, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and discoidal, with an involution of about 1/3 and a small umbilicus. The shell surface is ornamented with fine, dense transverse ribs, which arise at the umbilical wall and bifurcate at the umbilical tubercles, with many more bifurcating at the outer one-third of the flanks, the bifurcation points not forming tubercles, and a few single ribs inserted. On the phragmocone the ribs are fine and dense, mostly bifurcating. The body-chamber whorl has deep, wide constrictions crossing the venter. The suture is poorly preserved; a wide ventral saddle and a narrow, short ventral lateral lobe are visible; the first lateral lobe is wide and long, with a slender tail branch and symmetrical long lateral branches; the second lateral lobe is short and small. The external saddle is tall and wide, divided by a secondary lobe into two equal parts; the first lateral saddle is poorly preserved, apparently also divided by a secondary lobe into two equal parts; the auxiliary lobe is poorly preserved.

The venter is rounded, the flanks slightly convex, the ventrolateral margin bluntly rounded. The umbilical wall is steep, the umbilical margin rounded. The growth lines and ribs are parallel, with a wide, shallow lateral sinus, a narrow and deep ventral sinus and a distinct ventrolateral projection. The siphuncle lies close against the ventral shell wall. The external suture has a narrow, spear- shaped ventral lobe, a slightly wider lateral lobe and a short, small umbilical lobe. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Hujiertai, Hujiertai Township, Nilka County, Ili Kazakh Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is large, flattened globose and semi-involute. The outer whorl almost completely encloses the penultimate whorl, being impressed by the latter to two-thirds of the whorl height. The whorl width is slightly greater than the whorl height, and the whorl cross- section is semi-elliptical. The umbilicus is rather large and deep; the umbilical margin is rounded, the umbilical wall rather high and steep. The shell surface is ornamented with well-developed longitudinal spiral striae. Besides the longitudinal striae there are well- developed, slightly coarse, curved fold-like striae, which arise at the umbilical margin, first bending forwards and then bending backwards towards the outer part; the longitudinal and fold-like striae interweave into a net-like pattern. The outer whorl has 4-5 constrictions. The external suture has a rather wide ventral lobe, wider above and narrowing slightly downwards; the median saddle is moderately high, about one-half of the height of the ventral lobe; the ventral lateral lobe is wedge-shaped; the lateral lobe is short and wide, pointed at the lower end; the umbilical lobe is narrow and shallow, situated on the umbilical wall; the external saddle is rather narrow, with a narrow, pointed saddle top, inclined slightly towards the umbilicus; the lateral saddle is low and asymmetrical on the two sides.

The whorl height exceeds the thickness, the cross-section being a tall ellipse. The shell surface is ornamented with crest-like ribs extending obliquely forwards, arising at the umbilical margin; some ribs bifurcate at the mid-flanks, others do not bifurcate, the two kinds of ribs occurring almost alternately, and there are also cases of two single ribs between two bifurcating ribs. The ribs are densely and uniformly distributed, all terminating at the sides of the ventral groove, but the closer to the front end of the whorl, the weaker the ribs become on the venter, forming a distinct depression and crossing the venter; the whorl has distinct constrictions, but on the whorl the ribs weaken gradually on the venter, forming a distinct depression and crossing the venter.

species.distribution: Jiapila-Damala, Chamdo County, Chamdo Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Dawanpo, Longchang Town, Zhenfeng County, Qianxinan Bouyei and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is semi-involute and elliptical, with an arched, rounded venter and a very shallow ventral groove, apparently caused by the interruption of the transverse ribs at the venter. The whorl height grows rather slowly, the width rather rapidly, so that near the aperture of the last whorl the width is slightly greater than the height, forming a wide, ovate cross-section. The transverse ribs on the surface are robust and simple, radiate, with no bifurcation seen. With growth, the transverse ribs become sparser and more robust. The transverse ribs usually bear six rows of tubercles, the three rows on the venter and ventrolateral part being more prominent, especially the row along the margin of the ventral groove, which is particularly large; the two rows on the flanks and the row at the umbilical margin are weaker.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences, specimen no. 15591, resource no. F004003851; collected at Dawanpo, Longchang Town, Zhenfeng County, Qianxinan Bouyei and Miao Autonomous Prefecture, Guizhou Province, China. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Mt
species.diagnosis: The shell is semi-evolute, with a narrow, arched venter, flat flanks and a very tall whorl. The surface is ornamented with curved transverse ribs, which begin to bend forwards at the ventrolateral margin, are interrupted at the margin of the median ventral groove, and form a distinct row of ventrolateral tubercles. There is another row of tubercles at the umbilical margin. The umbilicus is medium-sized. The suture is subceratitic; the external lobe is very short and shallow, the lateral lobe wide and long, the umbilical lobe rather shallow and rounded. All the lobes are denticulate, invading the saddles only slightly and only in the lower part of the saddles.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: the mountain behind Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is large, rather thick, moderately involute, with a rather deep umbilicus and a not very steep umbilical wall. The venter is of medium width, with a wide and flat ventral groove. The flanks are flat, converging rather rapidly towards the venter on the outer side, the greatest whorl thickness being at the inner one-third, the cross-section subelliptical or nearly quadrate. The surface is ornamented with radiate ribs inclined forwards; the ribs arise at the umbilical margin and bifurcate at one-third of the way outwards, the short branch ribs gradually becoming independent of the main ribs and forming independent short ribs. In addition, there are single ribs arising at the umbilical margin without bifurcating. All kinds of ribs gradually widen from the inside outwards, terminating at the venter.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: west of Kadong Village, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is semi-evolute and thickly discoidal, with an involution of about 1/3. The umbilical diameter is 15 mm, the umbilical wall short and steeply inclined, the umbilical margin ornamented with indistinct umbilical tubercles. The flanks are flat, the venter flat and rounded, with a distinct ventral groove. At a diameter of 43 mm the whorl height is 17 mm and the thickness 14 mm, the cross-section not clear enough, apparently tall and quadrate. The shell surface is ornamented with dense ribs; most ribs bifurcate at the umbilical tubercles or the umbilical margin, one branch not bifurcating again, the other bifurcating again at the mid-flanks or slightly outside, the bifurcation point forming an indistinct tubercle-like projection. A few ribs bifurcate at the umbilical margin and do not bifurcate again on the flanks, and very few single ribs arise at the umbilical margin. All ribs terminate at the sides of the ventral groove, slightly swollen, without forming tubercles. The suture is indistinct, a wide first lateral lobe being faintly visible.

The flanks are arched and rounded, gradually narrowing towards the venter, the venter arc-shaped. The whorl height is less than the width, the cross-section being a flat ellipse. species.distribution: west of Kadong Village, Duoque District, Langkazi County, Shannan Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute and thick, with an involution of slightly less than 1/2, a steeply inclined umbilical wall and rather flat flanks. The whorl width and thickness are equal, the greatest thickness being at the umbilical margin, the venter flat and rounded, the cross- section a flat circle. The shell surface is ornamented with dense, coarse, radiate ribs and prominent umbilical tubercles; the ribs bifurcate from the umbilical tubercles, bifurcate again at the mid-flanks, extending slightly obliquely forwards, and meet the ribs of the other flank on the venter in a herringbone pattern, at a rather large angle. The shell surface has deep constrictions extending obliquely forwards. The suture is poorly preserved; a much-branched ventral lateral lobe is visible, and a wide, tall lateral saddle divided by a small leaflet into two equal parts. The first lateral lobe is short and wide, with undeveloped lateral branches.

species.distribution: Gucuo Village, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is small, evolute and thickly discoidal. It has six regularly increasing whorls, with an involution of 2/3. The umbilicus is wide and deep, conically depressed, with a steep umbilical wall and a rounded umbilical margin. The venter is broad and somewhat arched and rounded; the greatest whorl thickness lies at the tubercles, and the cross-section is nearly flat-elliptical. The surface bears bundled transverse ribs. Stout prismatic tubercles are distributed along the umbilical margin, becoming more prominent towards the outside; from the prismatic tubercles, 2-3 secondary ribs branch off at 1/3 of the way out from the umbilical margin, extending forward obliquely in bundles, and meeting on the two sides of the venter at a rather flat angle, forming a slight chevron pattern and becoming rather stout.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Kumudawan Gully, Turpan City, Turpan Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is rather large, flattened-globose and evolute, with 4-5 whorls. The whorls increase rather evenly, the outer whorl enclosing most of the next inner whorl. The whorl width far exceeds the whorl height, and the cross-section is crescent-shaped. The umbilicus is rather wide, slightly more than 1/3 of the shell diameter; the umbilical margin is subangular, the umbilicus deep and funnel-shaped; the shell surface is smooth. The external suture: the ventral lobe is rather wide, divided by a median saddle of medium height into two branch lobes; the ventral branch lobes bulge in the middle and taper downward, asymmetric on the two sides; the external saddle is wide and high, slightly constricted at the top and cap-shaped; the lateral lobe is longer than the ventral lobe, convex above and distinctly narrowing downward, with a pointed lower end; the lateral saddle is narrow and asymmetric, steeply inclined towards the umbilicus; the umbilical lobe lies on the umbilical wall.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is evolute, with five whorls; the flanks bear distinct ribs, about 14 in number. Not far from the venter there are commonly lateral tubercles and transverse ribs, and the venter bears a distinct median keel. The suture is of the ceratitic type; the external suture has two denticulate lateral lobes and a short auxiliary lobe series on each side. The ventral lobe is divided by a low ventral saddle into two pointed ventral branch lobes. The first lateral lobe is wide and deep, with many serrations at its end; the second lateral lobe is shorter and narrower, also serrated at its end, with fewer serrations than the first. All saddles are dome-shaped.
species.remarks: Illustrated specimen: Yifu Museum, China University of Geosciences (Wuhan), specimen no. YF0615, resource no. species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Penglaitan, Laibin City, Guangxi Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, semi-evolute and discoidal. The venter is apparently arched and rounded; the flanks are slightly convex, the greatest convexity lying in the middle- inner part of the flanks. The umbilicus is shallow and small, the umbilical wall low and sloping, and the umbilical margin rather rounded. The inner whorls bear fine rib-like tubercles on the flanks; with growth the rib-like tubercles become coarser and larger, becoming short stout transverse ribs in the middle-posterior part of the outer whorl, and towards the anterior the transverse ribs become longer and more closely spaced. All transverse ribs arise at the umbilical margin, slanting slightly backward, thickening near the ventrolateral margin and slanting forward, terminating at the ventrolateral part. The suture is of the ceratitic type.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Tulong, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell involute, sides slightly compressed. Venter arched and rounded, with a distinct median keel, flanked on each side by a shallow longitudinal groove. Greatest whorl width near the umbilical margin. Umbilicus small. Shell surface bears weak umbilical nodes and strongly curved coarse transverse ribs. The ribs bend forward at the ventrolateral margin and end at the longitudinal grooves on either side of the median ventral keel; the ribs of the two flanks do not meet across the venter.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Qingzhen City, Guiyang City, Guizhou Province, China
species.diagnosis: Shell large, evolute, thickly discoidal. Venter broadly arched and rounded, with a prominent median ventral keel. Whorl cross-section slightly inverted-trapezoidal. Flanks slope toward the umbilicus, tending to flatten toward the anterior part of the outer whorl. Umbilicus broad and deep, umbilical margin indistinct. On the ventrolateral margins of the posterior and middle parts of the outer whorl there are coarse, highly raised longitudinal nodes. The transverse ribs on the flanks are coarse and short; toward the anterior part of the outer whorl the longitudinal nodes weaken into nodes and the transverse ribs on the flanks also weaken. The first lateral lobe of the suture is rather broad, the first lateral saddle broad and deep with a gently rounded saddle top, the second lateral saddle higher, its outer upper part inclined toward the umbilicus.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Kalajila, Altay City, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Medium to fairly large shell, thickly discoidal to flattened globose, involute. The outer whorl embraces 5/6 of the preceding whorl and is impressed by the latter to 1/2 of the whorl height. Whorl height exceeds whorl width; the whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical. The shell surface bears fine, dense longitudinal striae and weak transverse striae. The outer whorl bears 2–3 constrictions. The external suture: the ventral lobe is moderately wide, wide in the upper part, slightly convex in the middle, and narrows abruptly at the median saddle; the median saddle occupies slightly less than 1/2 of the ventral lobe height; the ventral prongs are pointed, knife-like, slightly flaring outward; the lateral lobe is wide, asymmetrical on the two sides, pointed at the lower end; the umbilical lobe is narrow and pointed, situated on the umbilical wall; the external saddle is fairly wide, with a narrow, pointed top, low and oblique. During ontogeny the middle of the ventral lobe of the suture becomes gradually more convex, the median saddle becomes higher, the external saddle more pointed, and the lateral lobe longer.

species.diagnosis: Medium or fairly large shell, involute, flattened globose. The outer whorl embraces 2/3 of the height of the preceding whorl. The whorl is thickest at the umbilical margin, from which it slopes slightly outward and curves into the venter; the ventrolateral region is fairly rounded. Whorl width is slightly greater than whorl height or nearly equal; the whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical. The umbilicus is small and slightly deep; the shell surface bears transverse striae and very fine, dense longitudinal striae, about 30 or more longitudinal striae within a 10 mm interval. The external suture: the ventral lobe is moderately wide, divided by a moderately high median saddle into two spear-shaped ventral prongs that flare slightly outward; the lateral lobe is wider than the ventral lobe, with weak, rounded lateral projections on the two sides; the umbilical lobe is narrow and pointed, situated on the umbilical wall; the external saddle is moderately wide, high and pointed; the lateral saddle is low.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Mt
species.diagnosis: Shell involute, flattened discoidal, with a flattened venter bearing one median keel and two ventrolateral keels; fairly dense falcate transverse ribs, which sometimes bifurcate near the middle of the flank and bend sharply forward at the ventrolateral margin, forming a prominent ventrolateral keel. In adult specimens, each half whorl bears 28–38 transverse ribs. The umbilicus is fairly small, the umbilical wall fairly steep. The body chamber is at least three-quarters of a whorl long. The suture is subammonitic; the external lobe is very wide and shallow, generally half the depth of the lateral lobe; the external suture has four umbilical lobes, rarely three; all umbilical lobes are small and shallow. The external and lateral saddles are both fairly high, with many but shallow denticulations; the umbilical saddle is slightly wider and lower, with fewer denticulations.

species.diagnosis: Shell flattened discoidal, semi-involute, with a medium-sized umbilicus. The venter is arched and rounded; the flanks are flatly convex; the umbilicus is not deep; the whorl cross-section is nearly ovate. The suture: the ventral lobe is wide and rounded, slightly constricted in the front part, trifid, with fairly wide lateral prongs that are slightly pointed and rounded at the base; adult specimens bear denticulations. In early development the two sides of the ventral lobe are nearly parallel, and the frontal constriction is indistinct. The first lateral lobe is about as wide as the ventral lobe, rounded at the base, with small denticulations. The succeeding lobes are small and asymmetrical, with 6 lateral and umbilical lobes on each side in total.

species.distribution: about 2 km southeast of Langnongla Mountain, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Shell semi-evolute to semi-involute. The whorl cross-section is subtriangular. The surface bears fairly strong transverse ribs and a row of nodes. The transverse ribs protrude into spine-like nodes near the inner part of the middle of the flank, where they bifurcate and intercalate transverse ribs. The umbilicus is of medium size. The external lobe is fairly wide and short, bifid, with denticulations. The lateral lobe is wide and deep; the denticulations on the lateral and umbilical lobes are fine.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Mt
species.diagnosis: Discoidal shell, semi-involute to semi-evolute, the venter of the outer whorl flatly dome- shaped, the whorl cross-section slightly elongated hexagonal. The flanks bear sparse, short, coarse transverse ribs, which often form a transverse node at the most convex part of the flank; the ventrolateral margin bears a row of large ventrolateral nodes, sometimes longitudinally node-like. The body chamber is probably a whorl long. The suture is of the subceratitic type, comprising one wide, shallow external lobe, one very deep lateral lobe, five umbilical lobes and one very narrow internal lobe. The upper parts of the lobes are all constricted.

species.diagnosis: Large or fairly large shell, flattened globose, semi-involute. The outer whorl embraces most of the preceding whorl; whorl height and whorl width are roughly equal, the whorl cross-section nearly semi-lunar. The umbilicus is slightly large and deep, funnel-shaped. The shell surface of the posterior part of the outer whorl bears fine, dense longitudinal striae, about 30 striae within 15 mm in the middle of the venter; slightly sparse, curved transverse striae occur on the umbilical margin and flanks. The external suture: the ventral lobe is narrow and long, with nearly parallel sides, slightly constricted in the middle and widening upward; the median saddle is moderately high, about 1/2 of the ventral lobe length; the ventral prongs are pincer-shaped; the lateral lobe is long, slightly wider than the ventral lobe, wide above, with slightly convex sides, narrowing downward, narrow and pointed at the lower end; the umbilical lobe is narrow and long, situated on the umbilical wall, small funnel-shaped; the external saddle is high and fairly wide, with a top that is not pointed; the lateral saddle is wide and rounded, fairly low and asymmetrical on the two sides.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Nanmingyuexia, Chaotian Town, Guangyuan City, Sichuan Province, China
species.diagnosis: The shell of this species is semi-evolute to evolute and discoidal. The whorl height exceeds the width, and the cross-section is elliptical. The venter is arched and rounded, the flanks slightly convex. The umbilicus is large and shallow. The flanks of the inner whorls bear rounded nodes; as the whorls grow, the nodes gradually elongate transversely into ribs, the ribs starting from the umbilical margin, curving slightly backward, arranged radially, and inclining forward at the ventrolateral margin and gradually disappearing. The suture is of the ammonitic type; the external suture consists of a bifurcate ventral lobe, two lateral lobes and an auxiliary lobe series.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Tuyukerishi, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is fairly large and thinly discoidal. Semi-evolute, with 5-6 whorls. The venter is fairly broad and slightly arched, the ventrolateral margin rounded. The flanks are broad and flat, the two sides parallel. The umbilical margin is subangular, the umbilical wall fairly steep and slightly inclined. The shell surface appears smooth. The ventral lobe of the external suture is narrow, the median lobe being much longer than the ventral branches; the first lateral lobe is broad and short, its width more than twice that of the ventral lobe, and the secondary saddle of the 'lateral lobe' is low and rounded; the external saddle is low and arched; the tips of the other 'lateral lobes' all point vertically downward; the first 'lateral saddle' is the highest; the other saddles become successively lower.

species.distribution: Langnongla, Nyalam County, Shigatse Prefecture, Xizang Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: Discoidal, evolute shell, with a narrow, arched venter and fairly flat flanks. The venter and the ventrolateral part bear about 11 longitudinal spiral striae, with some short, shallow folds near the umbilical margin. The umbilicus is very small, with a fairly steep, straight umbilical wall. In the suture, the side of the external saddle near the venter tends to split, the external lobe becomes shallow, the lateral lobe is the deepest, and the saddles are conical.

species.classification: Ammonoidea (order and family not verified from NIMRF record)
species.distribution: Tuyukerishi, Altay Prefecture, Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region, China
species.diagnosis: The shell is of medium size, thickly discoidal and involute. The whorl width exceeds the whorl height, and the whorl cross-section is semi-elliptical. The umbilicus is small and fairly shallow; the shell surface shows a small reticulate pattern. The outer whorl bears 1-3 shallow constrictions. The ventral lobe of the external suture is moderately broad, widening slightly toward the aperture, divided by a moderately high median saddle into two narrow, pointed ventral branches; the lateral lobe is about as wide as the ventral lobe, its sides slightly convex; the umbilical lobe is short and shallow, located on the umbilical wall; the top of the external saddle is narrowly arched, and the lateral saddle is broader and lower.
